# KatLang Agent Instructions

## Project Overview

- These instructions are for Codex and other AI coding agents working in this repository.
- `AGENTS.md` is the canonical shared agent-instructions file for this repo.
- KatLang's authoritative language model is `lean/KatLang.lean`.
- The C# implementation in `src/KatLang/` must stay semantically aligned with Lean.
- If Lean and C# are both wrong for the same bug, fix both together when feasible.
- Keep this file operational and concise.

## Core Architecture

- `lean/KatLang.lean`: source of truth for AST shape, evaluation rules, and invariants.
- `lean/CoreTests.lean`, `lean/AstDemo.lean`: Lean-side regression and AST compatibility checks.
- `lean/CoreArityAlgebra.lean`, `lean/CoreArityAlgebraProofs.lean`, `lean/CoreArityAlgebra.md`: isolated paper-facing extraction of KatLang's arity algebra; it must stay faithful to `lean/KatLang.lean` but is not authoritative semantics.
- `src/KatLang/`: C# AST, parser, front-end elaboration, evaluator, diagnostics, and public API.
- `src/KatLang/Semantics/`: editor-facing semantic tooling only; it is not the evaluator and not the normative semantics layer.
- `tests/KatLang.Tests/`: parser, evaluator, elaboration, semantics, and integration regression coverage.
- `tutorial.md`, `KatLang.ebnf`, and generator prompt/agent files must stay aligned with real language behavior.
- `docs/design/language-rules/`: the full statement of every compact rule in this file (consequences, examples, implementation map, pinning tests), as binding as this file; its `README.md` says which file to read before touching which subsystem.

## Language Semantics And Design Rules

A bracketed pointer such as [`syntax.md` § The spread marker] names the section of `docs/design/language-rules/` that holds the full rule; read it before changing that rule's implementation, and change both together.

- Lean 4 wins over implementation convenience, performance, or stylistic preference.
- ALIAS-UNIFY-1: Q1–Q7 are the single production structural authority for detector, resolver, editor and exposure consumers. A1 reports statically unresolved self-dependent inference as deterministic `SelfDependentInferredParameters`, once per body with names in first-occurrence order. Replaced structural chases and inference deciders are deleted. Preserve M4★, OD-B–OD-E and NEED-04. B2 is not adopted; X-04 remains an owner decision. See `docs/design/static-structure-resolver-2026-10.md` § 9.
- B3 query implementation contract (IR-04): ordinary `Read` observes an information lower bound; `Follow` declares the entire, conclusive, stable single-successor reference equation. Never infer OD-D returns from evaluation ancestry or speculate a successor under Unknown. Keep graph representatives separate from language identities; require monotonicity/branch agreement, finite operation-scaled bounds and bounded callback/fan-in work before production use. Read `docs/design/static-structure-resolver-2026-10.md` § 3 before changing the engine or implementing its queries.
- B3-2★ query contracts: read `docs/design/static-structure-query-contracts-2026-10.md`. Receiver-expansion returns differ from target cycles; known name presence differs from unresolved binding identity. Branch regions belong in contextual keys. `IsModuleElaborated` marks loader expansion, not completed inference. RawSource admits inference/reference formation, NameResolved admits formation only, and Resolved admits neither; standalone consumers require explicit phase provenance.
- B3-2★ publication: editor, exposure, provenance and validators consume authoritative completed receiver/member and OD-C provider facts. Unavailable/pending facts never permit a raw chase. Exposure retargets declaration-preserving views before sealing. Immutable completed facts and deferred continuations retain no producer engine/token; unsuccessful units publish no successful completion.
- B3-2★ context boundary: register rewritten views separately from immutable definitions; materialized branches have fresh regions. Preserve genuine owner/branch/activation identity, contextual host-signature admission and shared-family publication. Freeze completed error-free units only. Q8 requirements/processing/MAY→MUST and Q9 pending/completed cells remain; their redesign belongs to B3-5★.
- B3-2★ resource policy: `SourceProcessingLimits.MaxStaticStructureBytes` configures a lower per-operation structural accounting envelope under a deterministic 1-GiB supported ceiling; GC memory never changes the default. Finite operation-scaled work/read bounds, entry limits and metadata accounting remain active. `StaticStructureLimitExceeded` is resource refusal, not an inference rule. Gate D final acceptance is conditional on fresh F1–F3 validation and independent delta review; see `experimental/features/alias-unify-1-b32-final-corrections-2026-10-30.md`. The scoped owner-approved exhaustive 44-batch V3 fallback preserves whole collections and exact cases under 900-second/6-GiB limits, with cross-class co-residency unproven.
- `lean/CoreArityAlgebra.lean` defines the algebra. `lean/CoreArityAlgebraProofs.lean` proves the small laws and executable checks. If either diverges from `lean/KatLang.lean`, fix the artifact or explicitly change the authoritative model first.
- If Lean is ambiguous for a requested behavior change, stop and clarify before implementing.
- Do not invent syntax or semantics that are not in Lean unless the task explicitly includes the Lean change.
- Do not add new operators, convenience syntax, implicit coercions, hidden fallbacks, or AST simplifications that erase Lean distinctions.
- Preserve structural distinctions in the AST and runtime model. In particular, `.dotCall` and `open` are language-level constructs, not incidental parser sugar.
- `Expr.SequenceConstruct` / `.sequenceConstruct` is an INTERNAL sequence-join node, not the AST representation of written parenthesized sequence values (those parse to `Expr.Capture` / `.capture` bundles; `()` to the empty-sequence node). Its evaluation drops non-spread `()` leaves (a spread leaf contributes exactly its spread items, like a spread row), so routing surface syntax through it would violate visible-empty semantics — the parser must never produce it (guarded by `SequenceConstructContainmentTests`, CoreTests internal-node guards, and the semantic explorer's internal-node cases; see `docs/design/sequence-boundary-audit-2026-07.md` §7).
- Brace algorithms parse to `Expr.AlgorithmExpr` / `.algorithmExpr` (algorithm identity); a surviving parenthesized group parses to `Expr.Capture` / `.capture` over an `OutputBundle` — ordered written slots with NO lexical ownership, consumed by the receiver. Capture is not algorithm identity (`Apply((Inc, Dec))` errors, `(Obj*).V` falls back, `open (M, N)` is `BadOpenForm`), while every `AlgorithmExpr` provides its algorithm on the higher-order channel whatever its parameter count — and a REDUNDANT group is not a capture at all (`Apply((Increment))` is `Apply(Increment)`, `(Obj).V` is `Obj.V`, `open (M)` is `open M`; see the parentheses bullet). `Expr.Call.Args` is an `OutputBundle` and `Expr.DotCall.Args` an optional one (`null` = property-style access), evaluated in the CALLER's context; there is no transparent Args algorithm and no `IsParametrized` mode bit — every `Algorithm.User` owns a scope (parser entry points `ParseScopedAlgorithm` / `ParseParenthesizedBodyParts`). Value-context lifting is a consumer property decided by the ONE role classifier of the unified formula-lifting law (`FormulaLiftingRoles`, bullet below): builtin value slots and Math, host and family arguments lift, a user callable's whole argument stays neutral, and a closed list leaves blocked lifting as runtime zero-argument demand (Model-C Q-15). [`sequences-lists-and-calls.md` § Output bundles, capture, and algorithm identity]
- MODEL-C CALL-BY-NEED (October 2026): one suspended/Ready NeedCell per supplied computation; plain binding, parameter transport, alias indirection and collector-slice opening do not force. First VALUE demand evaluates once in the caller environment, memoizing full counted success, ordinary failure or cancellation; overlapping demands join one flight. CALLABLE projection is independent and never forces the projected cell's VALUE (a RUNTIME projection — an `.Algorithm` link, META-S3-1 — may demand OTHER cells' VALUE on its callee route, as a node of the run's ONE wait-for graph; a runtime projection's FAILURE keeps its kind and is never read as absence). Inspecting patterns traverse left to right; families share one supply across attempts. Arbitrary spread forms eager Ready items; collector VALUE materializes the whole exact list. Cardinality precedes ordinary demand. The Lean binder (`bindNeedPatterns`, `selectNeedFamilyBranch`) is ONE generic TOTAL core (`NeedBinder`, R3) over a monad with `Error` exceptions and `NeedCapabilities` (VALUE demand, CALLABLE projection, cell allocation), defined above the `partial` evaluator block; the production names are BY DEFINITION its `EvalM` specializations at `NeedChannels.capabilities` (the block passes the total `NeedChannels.shell` over `demandNeedRecursive` / `projectNeedWrittenAt`, `bindingChannels` — one unfolding of the two drivers, S6a). Its top-level cardinality, allocation, minimum and plain-binding laws are theorems (`KatLangArityLaws.lean` § Model-C production binder laws, FORMAL-07), and so is its demand order — the per-pattern event schedule, the silence of plain non-repeated bindings at any position, the per-occurrence repeated-name order and verdict (Q-28's permutation/representative laws since S5, over stable completed contributions — on flat levels in `KatLangArityLaws/RepeatedNameLaws.lean`, on nested and mixed heads under the stated completed/Ready and initial identity-domain premises, with fresh-child provenance, since S6a in `NestedRepeatedNames.lean`, callable-identity transitivity off identified/anonymous printed fallbacks in `CallableIdentityDomain.lean`), first-failure truncation, family search and arbitrary-context activation — proved over the production `EvalM` runs and an external boundary trace that erases exactly to them (`KatLangArityLaws/BinderTrace.lean`, `FamilyDispatch.lean`; the opaque helpers' outcomes stay symbolic, and the recursive evaluator callers stay source facts; R5 totalizes supply control (`NeedSupply`) and collector/completion control (`NeedDemand`), with public specialization, address/provenance/order/failure and qualified heap laws in `KatLangArityLaws/NeedControl.lean`; `evalCounted` and the thin `demandNeedRecursive` edge remain partial, and whole-run heap refinement remains open). `BinderCorrespondence.lean` adds per-channel substitution (results depend on the channels only through the cells the run invokes), its static form (a head invokes its channels only on cells at inspecting positions or on cells the run allocated) and the family/ordinary mode correspondence for every head (the modes differ only where the ordinary binding raises an incompatibility; a literal-free head's ordinary binding is never a non-match); `SupplyCorrespondence.lean` (S5) proves the binder's heap-renaming simulation over corresponding supplies and the callback route's Ready-supply correspondence (the `partial` CALLABLE projection and recursive collector edge stay premises; a suspended written argument and its Ready value are NOT equivalent: CALLABLE and META differ). Never move it back into the block, and never add an observation field to `EvalState`. Cyclic active dependencies report DemandCycle; fresh recursion obeys ordinary limits. Q-15 blocked lifting is runtime demand, while directly written undeclared names and Q-77 structural incompatibility stay static. Cell work adds no semantic charge and property caching is a separate domain. RESULTS ARE CALCULATION VALUES: inputs may expose VALUE and CALLABLE, but no result construction (output rows, `if`/clause selection, collections, selection, spread results, loop state) exports CALLABLE — projection exists only for written references, Ready data has none — and an undersupplied call is an arity error, never partial application (`ResultValueBoundaryTests`, CoreTests `ModelC`). [`call-by-need.md` § Production implementation map; § Result boundary]
- CALL REFERENCES (CallReference S1, October 2026; Lean-first): a parameter declared `meta name` (a CONTEXTUAL modifier — `F(meta)` and `meta = 3` keep the ordinary name; valid only as a plain, fixed name written once at the top level of an ordinary explicit parameter list, else `InvalidMetaParameter` / preflight `IllegalInEval`; formula lifting gives callers an ORDINARY binding) binds the run-scoped VALUE `Result.CallReference` (Lean `Result.callRef`) of the SUPPLIED CALL's invocation plan. The ONE R3 binder reaches it in WRITTEN order (`NeedPattern.metaRef`, capability `NeedCapabilities.reference` = `NeedPlan.reference`: reify, then one Ready adapter), so capture is INERT (no target, argument VALUE, supply preparation or spread) and an earlier inspecting pattern's failure wins; only a WRITTEN INVOCATION is capturable — since META-S3-4 any call through a name, parameter or argumentless path and any argument-bearing dot edge (GENERALIZED CAPTURE below) — `NotAnAlgorithm "meta: not a supplied call computation"` otherwise, Ready references included; at a binding site that refusal (category and inner description unchanged) gains exactly one frame `while binding meta parameter '<name>'` (the declared META parameter, builtins' `step` included) and is positioned at the argument as written at that call — a forwarded parameter read is its own occurrence (META-DIAG-1/2); earlier inspecting failures, a direct `ReifyMeta`, later invocation-route refusals, cancellation and resource errors get no frame. One cell is one reference through any forwarding, before or after its VALUE; `==` is plan identity; a reference has no CALLABLE, members, number/Boolean/text view or ordering. `R.Invoke()` is a structural-miss dot intrinsic beside `.string` (J1: a declared `Invoke` member wins, no lexical fallback, never an implicit parameter; bare `R.Invoke` is `IllegalInEval`, `R.Invoke(8)` `ArityMismatch(0, 1)`): a FRESH execution of the captured call in its captured context over the plan's ONE sticky supply (same memoized argument cells, spreads once), never touching the original VALUE. A reference never leaves its run: run results, host-operation arguments and interpolation refuse it (`TypeMismatch`), and C#'s ONE ownership helper (`Evaluator.CheckCallReferenceOwnership`) refuses foreign, ended or terminal runs. C# retains plans per RUN under the J7 program gate (`AstStructuralPreflight.MayCaptureCalls`, tested by the run's structural preflight walk: any META capture/binder or deferred module region in the admitted graph, parent scopes included; decided once in `EvaluationBudget`), so META-free programs keep the ordinary route and fusion. `R.Algorithm` is META-S3-1's callable projection (below). `CallReferenceS1Tests`, `KatLangArityLaws/CallReference.lean`, `CallReferenceGuards.lean`. [`call-by-need.md` § Call references]
- ARGUMENT VIEWS (CallReference S2, October 2026; Lean-first): `R.Arguments` is a structural-miss dot intrinsic beside `Invoke` (a declared `Arguments` member wins, no lexical fallback, never an implicit parameter; any argument list, `R.Arguments()` included, is `IllegalInEval`) yielding the reference's ONE lazy, read-only view (Lean `Result.argView`, C# the `IsArgumentView` facet of `Result.CallReference`; `R.Arguments == R.Arguments`, `R != R.Arguments`, never invocable). Obtaining it is INERT. Every view operation reads the plan's ONE sticky supply (`NeedPlan.viewCells`: the recorded preparation or ONE formation shared with VALUE and `Invoke()`, target never resolved). `count` counts the effective supplied cells and demands none; selection validates each selector (`selectorIndex`) BEFORE the supply is read (`R.Arguments[]` reads nothing) and demands ONLY selected cells (`selectViewWith`); `first`/`last` likewise; every other collection builtin and `atoms` refuse a view as their whole collection (`TypeMismatch`). In an argument or selector supply, a spread whose LAST star opens a view TRANSPORTS the original cells (`NeedSupply.SpreadEval` = `evalSupplySpread`, `SpreadSupply.cells`; C# `FormSpreadSupplySlot`) — no copy, no Ready wrapper, no demand; any star that would open a view into values (value-position spreads, `F(V**)`) is `TypeMismatch`. A view obeys the reference's boundaries, and every view operation passes `CheckCallReferenceOwnership` before and after plan work. `CallReferenceS2Tests`, `KatLangArityLaws/ArgumentView.lean`, `ArgumentViewGuards.lean`. [`call-by-need.md` § Argument views]
- CALLABLE PROJECTION (META-S3-1, October 2026; Lean-first): `R.Algorithm` is a structural-miss dot intrinsic beside `Invoke`/`Arguments` (a declared `Algorithm` member wins in every position, no lexical fallback — `5.Algorithm` is `TypeMismatch` — never an implicit parameter; the receiver is read as `Invoke` reads it and must be a reference of THIS run) denoting the plan's ONE canonical CALLEE CELL (CR-13: its route's callee — the written callee, a member path, the `.Algorithm` link or an extension's fallback — supplied in the captured caller context — a parameter callee is that parameter's own cell — established lazily, after the route, inertly and compare-and-set retained; C# `InvocationPlan.CalleeCell`, Lean `NeedPlan.calleeCell`). CALLABLE use (supplied, forwarded, callback, loop step, callee `(R.Algorithm)(x)`) is the callee's CALLABLE; bare `R.Algorithm` is the callee's ordinary VALUE (cache, computation or arity rejection — never a callable Result); `R.Algorithm(args)` is a FRESH ordinary call with exactly `args` (`R.Algorithm()` supplies nothing; families re-dispatch by the new supply; the owner's activation is kept). A SUPPLIED `X.Algorithm` is ONE link cell with ONE receiver cell shared by its VALUE and CALLABLE (CR-15), its CALLABLE a RUNTIME projection under the S3-0a flight and S3-0b `ResolveAsync`; obtaining/projecting never executes the captured invocation, prepares its supply or touches its VALUE (CR-16), and receiver/decode/callee-route failures keep their kind (NEED-06). `R.Algorithm.n` is the extension call `n(R.Algorithm)`; `R.Algorithm(R.Arguments*)` is itself a written invocation, so `R.Algorithm(R.Arguments*).while` loops the captured step (META-S3-4). `A = R.Algorithm` is a RUNTIME-TARGET ALIAS since META-S3-2 (the RUNTIME-TARGET CALLABLE ALIASES bullet). Lean: the projection block lives in the evaluator recursion core so a link can demand VALUE; `projectParameterWith` is L2's typed parameter projection. `CallReferenceS3AlgorithmTests`, `CallReferenceS3CorpusTests`, `KatLangArityLaws/AlgorithmProjection.lean`, `AlgorithmProjectionGuards.lean`. [`call-by-need.md` § Callable projection]

- GENERALIZED CAPTURE (META-S3-4, October 2026; Lean-first; owner decisions D-1A/D-2A/D-4, consequences D-3/D-5): the capture domain is SYNTACTIC (C# `IsPlannableCall`, Lean `NeedPlan.callShape?`): a call whose callee is a name, parameter or argumentless dot path, or an argument-bearing dot edge `t.N(args)` (`t.N()` included) — `Box.Step(0)`, `Math.Abs(-3)`, `(Box.G)(1)`, `5.Add(1)`, `Box.V()`, `op.Algorithm(op.Arguments*)`; an argumentless edge (`Box.G`, `5.Inc`), a name or a property read (`Start`, no implicit provenance) is not (D-2A). Capture stays inert. Each plan has ONE lazily decided ROUTE (`PlanRouteOf`/`PlanRouteOfAsync`, Lean `NeedPlan.routeOf`; first writer wins; a failure is retained, never absence) — call, member (callee the argumentless path, DOT-09), `.Algorithm` (callee the link; its ONE retained receiver cell keeps the ordinary invocation receiver evaluator and is shared by VALUE, `Invoke()`, `.Algorithm` and loops, D-3), extension (`5.Add(1)` is `Add(5, 1)`: the receiver is the FIRST supplied argument, D-5) or non-callable intrinsic (`5.string()`, `R.Invoke()`, `R.Arguments(…)`: VALUE is the ordinary evaluation, while invocation, `.Algorithm`, argument-supply reads and loop setup refuse with `NotAnAlgorithm "meta: not a callable invocation"`; capture, `==`, obtaining the view and empty selection stay inert, D-1A) — decided by THE ONE dot decision shared with ordinary dot evaluation (C# `SelectDotEdge`/`DotEdgeRoute` in `EvalDotCallCounted`, its async twin, `IsAlgorithmIntrinsicRoute` and `ComputePlanRoute`; Lean `selectDotEdge`). Reading the argument SUPPLY establishes the route first (D-4: identity resolution, which through a runtime-projection receiver performs that receiver's existing demand, before `repeat`'s count, RP-1). Name/parameter/path calls derive the call route from their source (no route object; plans gain one route field). `InvocationRoute/*Tests` (corpus of 164 programs × 3 engines, 35 ordinary/planned pairs, 216 MaxSteps scans), `KatLangArityLaws/InvocationRoute.lean`, `InvocationRouteGuards.lean`. [`call-by-need.md` § Generalized capture]
- HOST-ALIAS-R14: in C#, an alias declared directly in an ownerless host `ScopeCtx` keys its binding-cell memo, target memo and cycle identity on that declaring scope object by reference (D3-B), while rebuilt evaluator-owned declaring scopes retain structural identity; since HOST-NESTED-1 every ownerless host ANCESTOR on the chain (property-cache owners and alias memos alike) also counts by object reference. Alias-cell reuse never substitutes for a fresh eligible invocation; Lean's structural host identity remains the deferred O-6 boundary. [`ownership-and-lookup.md` § Runtime-target callable aliases]
- Algorithm output is written as expression rows: every non-definition expression row in an algorithm body contributes to that algorithm's output, and output rows may be interleaved with property definitions. There is no output keyword; `Output` and `output` are ordinary identifiers.
- PARENTHESES GROUP SYNTAX; THEY DO NOT INTRODUCE A SEMANTIC BOUNDARY (September 2026): a parenthesized group whose content is exactly ONE non-spread expression slot is that expression, whatever its kind — `(x)`, `((x))`, `(~x)`, `(F(1))`, `(Obj.X)`, `(A[0])`, `([1, 2])`, `({...})`, `((1, 2))`, `(())` elaborate to the very node `x`, `F(1)`, `Obj.X`, `A[0]`, `[1, 2]`, `{...}`, `(1, 2)`, `()` do (`Parser.IsRedundantGrouping`, the ONE decision, which never looks at the inner kind; the unwrapped node takes the group's extent as its span except that a NAME occurrence keeps its exact identifier span for the semantic model). ### Subagents

Do not delegate test execution. Measured in September 2026, a validation worker spent 30–50 requests to run two or three commands — about ten times the cost of running them inline — could not work in parallel with a tree that must stay frozen, and shared no prompt cache with the primary agent (caches are model-scoped and prefix-exact). A subagent is for a BULKY, SELF-CONTAINED INVESTIGATION whose intermediate reading would otherwise flood the primary context — a failure hunt across many files, an inventory, a cross-file audit. Give it the cheapest model that can do the job, a bounded brief with an explicit stopping point, and ask for `file:line` facts; code the primary agent will edit or reason about it reads itself, in bounded ranges. Never spawn one for a single known file, and never let one edit, regenerate, or validate.

## Continuous Integration And Releases

- `.github/workflows/validate.yml` is automatic for pull requests and pushes to
  `main`, and can also be dispatched manually. Its stable required-check names
  are `.NET validation` and `Lean validation`; both invoke the phase boundary
  above rather than duplicating commands in YAML. It runs BOTH phases on every
  such event regardless of which files changed — the full .NET + Lean backstop
  behind the risk-based local levels in `Validation` — and it never substitutes
  for a locally required V3.
- `validate-all.ps1` writes a command/exit-code/environment record, one TRX per
  test project, a failure summary and the GC-isolated allocation logs to a fresh
  git-ignored `artifacts/validation/validate-all-*` directory (a temporary
  directory if that path is not ignored). `validate.yml` uploads it with
  `if: always()`; the job result remains the validation result.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` is manual-only. Dispatch it from `main` with
  the version already present in `KatLangVersion.props`. A push, merge, or tag
  never publishes a release automatically.
- The release workflow validates the exact dispatched commit, builds and runs
  the NativeAOT CLI on native Windows/Linux/macOS x64 and ARM64 runners,
  packages the tested executable with the root `LICENSE`, `NOTICE`, and
  `PATENTS` files plus the exact restored RID-specific .NET runtime pack's MIT
  license and third-party notices, collects all six archives, produces
  `SHA256SUMS`, and only then creates the tag and publishes the GitHub Release.
  Runtime/ILCompiler pack identities and versions come from the publish output's
  `project.assets.json`, never from the machine-wide SDK root. The shipped
  projects currently have no external `PackageReference`; adding one requires
  explicit release-notice review and an update to the pinned CI policy. Unix
  archives store the CLI as mode `0755` and every text document as mode `0644`.
- `KatLangVersion.props` remains authoritative. Workflow code must never pass
  an MSBuild version override, create/move an existing version tag, or replace
  an existing release.
- Normal jobs have `contents: read`. Only the final publication job has
  `contents: write`; workflows use no user-managed secrets. External actions
  are pinned to immutable commit SHAs and `.github/dependabot.yml` proposes
  reviewable GitHub Actions pin updates.


## Public API Baseline And Release Version

- `tests/KatLang.Formatting.PublicApi.Tests/PublicApiBaseline.txt` is the checked-in, deterministic rendering of the COMPILED public surface of the `KatLang` assembly — the one assembly the NuGet package ships — reflected by `PublicApiSurfaceRenderer` in that deliberately non-friend test project: every exported type plus consumer-reachable protected nested types, with base/interfaces, generics and constraints; every consumer-visible member with parameter names, modifiers, defaults, nullable annotations and nullable-flow attributes; and every public enum member with its exact numeric value. `PublicApiBaselineTests` compares exactly and never rewrites; a difference is a NuGet surface change. Record an intentional change by regenerating it (`Regenerating generated artifacts` under `Validation`) and review the diff as the compatibility review. Regenerating the baseline never changes the release version; the focused hand-written contracts in that project (`PublicElaborationSurfaceTests`, `PublicFormatterExtensionTests`, `HostApiContractTests`) stay beside it.
- The public surface is LAYERED and deliberate (September 2026 public API audit): the primary host API (`KatLangEngine`, `RunOptions`, `RunResult`, `Result`, `KatLangError`/`KatLangErrorCode`), host extensibility (`HostOperation`/`HostOperations`, `OutputFormatter`/`BoundedOutputWriter`), analysis (`Parser`, `Lexer`/`Token`, `Semantics`), and the low-level `Evaluator` over the Lean-shaped AST — which evaluates a host-built `Expr` as-is and is never a source runner. Implementation machinery stays internal and is pinned so by name in `HostApiContractTests` (a baseline regeneration cannot bless re-exposing it): the signature and binding planners (`Signatures/`), the evaluator's value views on `Result` (spread/structure/selection/value-count views, `Normalize`, the UNBOUNDED atom projections — hosts use the bounded `RunResult.Success.Atoms` / `Evaluator.RunFlat`), `SemanticModel` construction, message builders, and compatibility shims. Source, evaluator, and configuration entry points validate their direct CLR arguments (host-built AST payloads remain an advanced caller contract) (`ArgumentNullException`, never a `NullReferenceException`); async entry points deliver every exception through the returned task; each `Evaluator` entry family has exactly one overload per arity (no positional-`null` ambiguity). `RunResult` variants and `ParseResult` are library-produced records with internal constructors and get-only payloads; hosts read/deconstruct them and construct `Result` values for host callbacks. `RunFlat`/`RunFlatAsync` accept host operations through the same bounded projection as their ordinary forms. The package ships its XML documentation — any documentation diagnostic that means a comment is wrong (unresolvable or ambiguous cref, bad param/paramref) is a build error, so docs cannot name a removed API — and is `IsAotCompatible` (trim/AOT analyzers on every build).
- `KatLangVersion.props` is the ONE place the release version is written. `src/KatLang/KatLang.csproj` (package and assembly version), `src/KatLang.CLI/KatLang.CLI.csproj` (which builds against the KatLang PROJECT, so it cannot lag onto a previously published package) and `tests/KatLang.CLI.Tests` (which bakes the value in as `IntendedKatLangVersion` assembly metadata — build intent, never read from the KatLang assembly under test) derive from it. `ReleaseVersionSourceTests` rejects any other version literal in an MSBuild file and any in-repository `PackageReference` to KatLang; the CLI version tests compare the loaded runtime, the CLI assembly and `--version` against the intended metadata, so a stale or mismatched artifact fails rather than passing against itself.

## Executable Language Specification

- `tests/KatLang.Tests/LanguageSpec/LanguageSpecCorpus.cs` is the canonical executable specification: named cases with stable IDs and HAND-WRITTEN canonical expectations. Never regenerate its expectations from observed behavior — a failing `LanguageSpec*` test means either fix the implementation or edit the canonical case in a reviewed diff.
- Same-program fidelity: the Lean program of every Lean-comparable case in BOTH differential corpora (`LanguageSpecCorpus` and `SemanticExplorerCorpus`, internal-node cases included) is DERIVED from the source's real elaborated AST through `tests/KatLang.Tests/LeanAstEncoder.cs` — never authored by hand and never rebuilt by test-side parser-rule templates. C#-only cases carry an explicit non-blank `LeanExclusionReason`, a hand-authored LanguageSpec Lean program requires the exceptional `LeanProgramOverride` + `LeanOverrideReason` (currently unused), and per-corpus exact-ID exclusions plus `FidelityRatchet_*` tests pin the derived-case partitions. The host-built AST corpus `HostParentDifferentialCorpus` (HOST-DIFF-1, pre-wired `ScopeCtx` parents, `lean/CoreTests/HostParentDifferential.lean`) encodes the SAME constructed graph C# evaluates, with exact-ID known HOST-LEAN-O6 divergences pinned on both sides. The encoder is FAIL-LOUD: extend it deliberately (with reviewed goldens in `LeanAstEncoderTests`) rather than approximating, and expected strings in encoder tests are manually reviewed constants. See `docs/design/executable-language-spec.md` §5.
- GENERATED from it (do not edit by hand): `lean/LanguageSpecCases.lean` and the `=== BEGIN GENERATED: katlang-spec-examples ===` block in both generator files; regenerate all three together (`Regenerating generated artifacts` under `Validation`). `lean/SemanticExplorerCases.lean` is the second GENERATED Lean/C# differential corpus (from `SemanticExplorerCorpus`; see `docs/design/sequence-boundary-audit-2026-07.md`): a failing `#guard` there is a Lean/C# divergence — or a Lean-internal plain/counted mismatch — on that case; after an intentional semantics change regenerate it the same way.
- Tutorial examples marked `<!-- spec:case-id -->` are verified against the corpus (source and expected output) by `TutorialSpecTests`; when changing a linked example, update the canonical case and the tutorial together.
- EVERY tutorial fence followed by a `**Result(s):**` claim is executable documentation: `TutorialResultSweepTests` runs it through `KatLangEngine.Run` and display-matches the claim — no marker needed, so an ordinary new example enters the sweep automatically. A genuinely non-standalone example (e.g. one needing a network downloader) carries `<!-- spec:skip nonblank reason -->` before the fence; the skip inventory is exact-pinned, and result-bearing coverage is monotonic (pinned minimum baseline — removing an existing claim requires a reviewed ratchet reduction, while additions need no pin edit). The shared grammar lives in `TutorialCorpus` and fails loudly on malformed/detached claims, so a result claim can never silently drop out of verification.
- Output-only verification is not a semantic pin (SYN-12): a tutorial example can print the documented number for the wrong reason (an indented `Inner = v + 1` beneath `Outer(v) = Inner` is a ROOT property whose `v` is forwarded through the closed list, not a nested property reading the parameter of its owner). The high-risk explanations — lexical ownership, visibility/export, property-first dot-call resolution, clause-family arity, sequence-value pattern kinds, the call/value boundary, Grace order — are therefore ALSO pinned by `tests/KatLang.Tests/LanguageSpec/TutorialSemanticContractTests.cs` through the elaborated AST (`Property.Exposure`, `Params`), the semantic model (`FindResolutionAt` declaration spans), and structured `DiagnosticCode`/`KatLangErrorCode` values; extend it, and the corpus, when such an explanation changes.
- When language behavior intentionally changes, update the affected canonical cases in the same task as the Lean/C#/tutorial/generator changes.
- Maintainer guide: `docs/design/executable-language-spec.md` (partitions, counts, how to add cases, worked example).

## Do Not

- Do not silently change language semantics.
- Do not let Lean and C# diverge.
- Do not treat `AGENTS.md` as a long design essay.
- Do not let multiple agent-instruction files drift into conflicting guidance.
- Do not add convenience syntax, hidden fallbacks, or duplicated semantic logic just to make a local change easier.
- Do not report a partial, stale, zero-test, or tool-blocked run as validation, and do not lower a selected validation level silently.
- Do not run validation commands concurrently or twice: one command in flight, one plan per candidate, no pre-validation sweep, and no subagent for test execution.
- Do not let a subagent edit code, tests, expectations, or tracked artifacts, run validation, or stage, commit, reset, or discard files.

FE-4a review: immutable required-ancestor backing is shared behind distinct nonempty property wrappers, preserving generated record equality/hash behavior; raw LocalOnlyProperty text prints bounded contents. Repeated open-head conditions reduce only under established lexical absence, retaining ambiguity and bound-owner rules. Large-base unions preserve shared cores. See evaluator-and-hosting.md, FE-4a hostile-review compatibility and cycle repairs.

EXPOSURE-OPEN-1: resolved open candidates use exact deep facts and interned seed keys; changed transforms share nodes per operation, same-shape references unite seeds, and completed expansions/settlements share only within fixed summary contexts. Never cache a partial cycle-cut expansion or settlement. See evaluator-and-hosting.md, EXPOSURE-OPEN-1.

# KatLang Agent Instructions

## Project Overview

- These instructions are for Codex and other AI coding agents working in this repository.
- `AGENTS.md` is the canonical shared agent-instructions file for this repo.
- KatLang's authoritative language model is `lean/KatLang.lean`.
- The C# implementation in `src/KatLang/` must stay semantically aligned with Lean.
- If Lean and C# are both wrong for the same bug, fix both together when feasible.
- Keep this file operational and concise.

## Core Architecture

- `lean/KatLang.lean`: source of truth for AST shape, evaluation rules, and invariants.
- `lean/CoreTests.lean`, `lean/AstDemo.lean`: Lean-side regression and AST compatibility checks.
- `lean/CoreArityAlgebra.lean`, `lean/CoreArityAlgebraProofs.lean`, `lean/CoreArityAlgebra.md`: isolated paper-facing extraction of KatLang's arity algebra; it must stay faithful to `lean/KatLang.lean` but is not authoritative semantics.
- `src/KatLang/`: C# AST, parser, front-end elaboration, evaluator, diagnostics, and public API.
- `src/KatLang/Semantics/`: editor-facing semantic tooling only; it is not the evaluator and not the normative semantics layer.
- `tests/KatLang.Tests/`: parser, evaluator, elaboration, semantics, and integration regression coverage.
- `tutorial.md`, `KatLang.ebnf`, and generator prompt/agent files must stay aligned with real language behavior.
- `docs/design/language-rules/`: the full statement of every compact rule in this file (consequences, examples, implementation map, pinning tests), as binding as this file; its `README.md` says which file to read before touching which subsystem.

## Language Semantics And Design Rules

A bracketed pointer such as [`syntax.md` § The spread marker] names the section of `docs/design/language-rules/` that holds the full rule; read it before changing that rule's implementation, and change both together.

- Lean 4 wins over implementation convenience, performance, or stylistic preference.
- ALIAS-UNIFY-1: Q1–Q7 are the single production structural authority for detector, resolver, editor and exposure consumers. A1 reports statically unresolved self-dependent inference as deterministic `SelfDependentInferredParameters`, once per body with names in first-occurrence order. Replaced structural chases and inference deciders are deleted. Preserve M4★, OD-B–OD-E and NEED-04. B2 is not adopted; X-04 remains an owner decision. See `docs/design/static-structure-resolver-2026-10.md` § 9.
- B3 query implementation contract (IR-04): ordinary `Read` observes an information lower bound; `Follow` declares the entire, conclusive, stable single-successor reference equation. Never infer OD-D returns from evaluation ancestry or speculate a successor under Unknown. Keep graph representatives separate from language identities; require monotonicity/branch agreement, finite operation-scaled bounds and bounded callback/fan-in work before production use. Read `docs/design/static-structure-resolver-2026-10.md` § 3 before changing the engine or implementing its queries.
- B3-2★ query contracts: read `docs/design/static-structure-query-contracts-2026-10.md`. Receiver-expansion returns differ from target cycles; known name presence differs from unresolved binding identity. Branch regions belong in contextual keys. `IsModuleElaborated` marks loader expansion, not completed inference. RawSource admits inference/reference formation, NameResolved admits formation only, and Resolved admits neither; standalone consumers require explicit phase provenance.
- B3-2★ publication: editor, exposure, provenance and validators consume authoritative completed receiver/member and OD-C provider facts. Unavailable/pending facts never permit a raw chase. Exposure retargets declaration-preserving views before sealing. Immutable completed facts and deferred continuations retain no producer engine/token; unsuccessful units publish no successful completion.
- B3-2★ context boundary: register rewritten views separately from immutable definitions; materialized branches have fresh regions. Preserve genuine owner/branch/activation identity, contextual host-signature admission and shared-family publication. Freeze completed error-free units only. Q8 requirements/processing/MAY→MUST and Q9 pending/completed cells remain; their redesign belongs to B3-5★.
- B3-2★ resource policy: `SourceProcessingLimits.MaxStaticStructureBytes` configures a lower per-operation structural accounting envelope under a deterministic 1-GiB supported ceiling; GC memory never changes the default. Finite operation-scaled work/read bounds, entry limits and metadata accounting remain active. `StaticStructureLimitExceeded` is resource refusal, not an inference rule. Gate D final acceptance is conditional on fresh F1–F3 validation and independent delta review; see `experimental/features/alias-unify-1-b32-final-corrections-2026-10-30.md`. The scoped owner-approved exhaustive 44-batch V3 fallback preserves whole collections and exact cases under 900-second/6-GiB limits, with cross-class co-residency unproven.
- `lean/CoreArityAlgebra.lean` defines the algebra. `lean/CoreArityAlgebraProofs.lean` proves the small laws and executable checks. If either diverges from `lean/KatLang.lean`, fix the artifact or explicitly change the authoritative model first.
- If Lean is ambiguous for a requested behavior change, stop and clarify before implementing.
- Do not invent syntax or semantics that are not in Lean unless the task explicitly includes the Lean change.
- Do not add new operators, convenience syntax, implicit coercions, hidden fallbacks, or AST simplifications that erase Lean distinctions.
- Preserve structural distinctions in the AST and runtime model. In particular, `.dotCall` and `open` are language-level constructs, not incidental parser sugar.
- `Expr.SequenceConstruct` / `.sequenceConstruct` is an INTERNAL sequence-join node, not the AST representation of written parenthesized sequence values (those parse to `Expr.Capture` / `.capture` bundles; `()` to the empty-sequence node). Its evaluation drops non-spread `()` leaves (a spread leaf contributes exactly its spread items, like a spread row), so routing surface syntax through it would violate visible-empty semantics — the parser must never produce it (guarded by `SequenceConstructContainmentTests`, CoreTests internal-node guards, and the semantic explorer's internal-node cases; see `docs/design/sequence-boundary-audit-2026-07.md` §7).
- Brace algorithms parse to `Expr.AlgorithmExpr` / `.algorithmExpr` (algorithm identity); a surviving parenthesized group parses to `Expr.Capture` / `.capture` over an `OutputBundle` — ordered written slots with NO lexical ownership, consumed by the receiver. Capture is not algorithm identity (`Apply((Inc, Dec))` errors, `(Obj*).V` falls back, `open (M, N)` is `BadOpenForm`), while every `AlgorithmExpr` provides its algorithm on the higher-order channel whatever its parameter count — and a REDUNDANT group is not a capture at all (`Apply((Increment))` is `Apply(Increment)`, `(Obj).V` is `Obj.V`, `open (M)` is `open M`; see the parentheses bullet). `Expr.Call.Args` is an `OutputBundle` and `Expr.DotCall.Args` an optional one (`null` = property-style access), evaluated in the CALLER's context; there is no transparent Args algorithm and no `IsParametrized` mode bit — every `Algorithm.User` owns a scope (parser entry points `ParseScopedAlgorithm` / `ParseParenthesizedBodyParts`). Value-context lifting is a consumer property decided by the ONE role classifier of the unified formula-lifting law (`FormulaLiftingRoles`, bullet below): builtin value slots and Math, host and family arguments lift, a user callable's whole argument stays neutral, and a closed list leaves blocked lifting as runtime zero-argument demand (Model-C Q-15). [`sequences-lists-and-calls.md` § Output bundles, capture, and algorithm identity]
- MODEL-C CALL-BY-NEED (October 2026): one suspended/Ready NeedCell per supplied computation; plain binding, parameter transport, alias indirection and collector-slice opening do not force. First VALUE demand evaluates once in the caller environment, memoizing full counted success, ordinary failure or cancellation; overlapping demands join one flight. CALLABLE projection is independent and never forces the projected cell's VALUE (a RUNTIME projection — an `.Algorithm` link, META-S3-1 — may demand OTHER cells' VALUE on its callee route, as a node of the run's ONE wait-for graph; a runtime projection's FAILURE keeps its kind and is never read as absence). Inspecting patterns traverse left to right; families share one supply across attempts. Arbitrary spread forms eager Ready items; collector VALUE materializes the whole exact list. Cardinality precedes ordinary demand. The Lean binder (`bindNeedPatterns`, `selectNeedFamilyBranch`) is ONE generic TOTAL core (`NeedBinder`, R3) over a monad with `Error` exceptions and `NeedCapabilities` (VALUE demand, CALLABLE projection, cell allocation), defined above the `partial` evaluator block; the production names are BY DEFINITION its `EvalM` specializations at `NeedChannels.capabilities` (the block passes the total `NeedChannels.shell` over `demandNeedRecursive` / `projectNeedWrittenAt`, `bindingChannels` — one unfolding of the two drivers, S6a). Its top-level cardinality, allocation, minimum and plain-binding laws are theorems (`KatLangArityLaws.lean` § Model-C production binder laws, FORMAL-07), and so is its demand order — the per-pattern event schedule, the silence of plain non-repeated bindings at any position, the per-occurrence repeated-name order and verdict (Q-28's permutation/representative laws since S5, over stable completed contributions — on flat levels in `KatLangArityLaws/RepeatedNameLaws.lean`, on nested and mixed heads under the stated completed/Ready and initial identity-domain premises, with fresh-child provenance, since S6a in `NestedRepeatedNames.lean`, callable-identity transitivity off identified/anonymous printed fallbacks in `CallableIdentityDomain.lean`), first-failure truncation, family search and arbitrary-context activation — proved over the production `EvalM` runs and an external boundary trace that erases exactly to them (`KatLangArityLaws/BinderTrace.lean`, `FamilyDispatch.lean`; the opaque helpers' outcomes stay symbolic, and the recursive evaluator callers stay source facts; R5 totalizes supply control (`NeedSupply`) and collector/completion control (`NeedDemand`), with public specialization, address/provenance/order/failure and qualified heap laws in `KatLangArityLaws/NeedControl.lean`; `evalCounted` and the thin `demandNeedRecursive` edge remain partial, and whole-run heap refinement remains open). `BinderCorrespondence.lean` adds per-channel substitution (results depend on the channels only through the cells the run invokes), its static form (a head invokes its channels only on cells at inspecting positions or on cells the run allocated) and the family/ordinary mode correspondence for every head (the modes differ only where the ordinary binding raises an incompatibility; a literal-free head's ordinary binding is never a non-match); `SupplyCorrespondence.lean` (S5) proves the binder's heap-renaming simulation over corresponding supplies and the callback route's Ready-supply correspondence (the `partial` CALLABLE projection and recursive collector edge stay premises; a suspended written argument and its Ready value are NOT equivalent: CALLABLE and META differ). Never move it back into the block, and never add an observation field to `EvalState`. Cyclic active dependencies report DemandCycle; fresh recursion obeys ordinary limits. Q-15 blocked lifting is runtime demand, while directly written undeclared names and Q-77 structural incompatibility stay static. Cell work adds no semantic charge and property caching is a separate domain. RESULTS ARE CALCULATION VALUES: inputs may expose VALUE and CALLABLE, but no result construction (output rows, `if`/clause selection, collections, selection, spread results, loop state) exports CALLABLE — projection exists only for written references, Ready data has none — and an undersupplied call is an arity error, never partial application (`ResultValueBoundaryTests`, CoreTests `ModelC`). [`call-by-need.md` § Production implementation map; § Result boundary]
- CALL REFERENCES (CallReference S1, October 2026; Lean-first): a parameter declared `meta name` (a CONTEXTUAL modifier — `F(meta)` and `meta = 3` keep the ordinary name; valid only as a plain, fixed name written once at the top level of an ordinary explicit parameter list, else `InvalidMetaParameter` / preflight `IllegalInEval`; formula lifting gives callers an ORDINARY binding) binds the run-scoped VALUE `Result.CallReference` (Lean `Result.callRef`) of the SUPPLIED CALL's invocation plan. The ONE R3 binder reaches it in WRITTEN order (`NeedPattern.metaRef`, capability `NeedCapabilities.reference` = `NeedPlan.reference`: reify, then one Ready adapter), so capture is INERT (no target, argument VALUE, supply preparation or spread) and an earlier inspecting pattern's failure wins; only a WRITTEN INVOCATION is capturable — since META-S3-4 any call through a name, parameter or argumentless path and any argument-bearing dot edge (GENERALIZED CAPTURE below) — `NotAnAlgorithm "meta: not a supplied call computation"` otherwise, Ready references included; at a binding site that refusal (category and inner description unchanged) gains exactly one frame `while binding meta parameter '<name>'` (the declared META parameter, builtins' `step` included) and is positioned at the argument as written at that call — a forwarded parameter read is its own occurrence (META-DIAG-1/2); earlier inspecting failures, a direct `ReifyMeta`, later invocation-route refusals, cancellation and resource errors get no frame. One cell is one reference through any forwarding, before or after its VALUE; `==` is plan identity; a reference has no CALLABLE, members, number/Boolean/text view or ordering. `R.Invoke()` is a structural-miss dot intrinsic beside `.string` (J1: a declared `Invoke` member wins, no lexical fallback, never an implicit parameter; bare `R.Invoke` is `IllegalInEval`, `R.Invoke(8)` `ArityMismatch(0, 1)`): a FRESH execution of the captured call in its captured context over the plan's ONE sticky supply (same memoized argument cells, spreads once), never touching the original VALUE. A reference never leaves its run: run results, host-operation arguments and interpolation refuse it (`TypeMismatch`), and C#'s ONE ownership helper (`Evaluator.CheckCallReferenceOwnership`) refuses foreign, ended or terminal runs. C# retains plans per RUN under the J7 program gate (`AstStructuralPreflight.MayCaptureCalls`, tested by the run's structural preflight walk: any META capture/binder or deferred module region in the admitted graph, parent scopes included; decided once in `EvaluationBudget`), so META-free programs keep the ordinary route and fusion. `R.Algorithm` is META-S3-1's callable projection (below). `CallReferenceS1Tests`, `KatLangArityLaws/CallReference.lean`, `CallReferenceGuards.lean`. [`call-by-need.md` § Call references]
- ARGUMENT VIEWS (CallReference S2, October 2026; Lean-first): `R.Arguments` is a structural-miss dot intrinsic beside `Invoke` (a declared `Arguments` member wins, no lexical fallback, never an implicit parameter; any argument list, `R.Arguments()` included, is `IllegalInEval`) yielding the reference's ONE lazy, read-only view (Lean `Result.argView`, C# the `IsArgumentView` facet of `Result.CallReference`; `R.Arguments == R.Arguments`, `R != R.Arguments`, never invocable). Obtaining it is INERT. - Do not silently change language semantics.

23:## Language Semantics And Design Rules
29:- B3 query implementation contract (IR-04): ordinary `Read` observes an information lower bound; `Follow` declares the entire, conclusive, stable single-successor reference equation. Never infer OD-D returns from evaluation ancestry or speculate a successor under Unknown. Keep graph representatives separate from language identities; require monotonicity/branch agreement, finite operation-scaled bounds and bounded callback/fan-in work before production use. Read `docs/design/static-structure-resolver-2026-10.md` § 3 before changing the engine or implementing its queries.

Gate D final acceptance is conditional on fresh F1–F3 validation and independent delta review; see `experimental/features/alias-unify-1-b32-final-corrections-2026-10-30.md`. 59:- INFERRED SIGNATURES ARE HELD TO THE RULES OF WRITTEN ONES (X-02, decided September 30 2026): a signature the front end composes must be one a programmer could write — ONE validator (`ParameterPattern.FindSignatureViolation`, Lean `ParameterPattern.signatureViolation?`; the singleton rule, one collecting parameter per pattern level, no repeated name including a collector) decides a written head, an inferred one (from shared template facts, `TemplateFacts.SignatureViolation`), and all three rules for a host-built user signature before evaluation (`PreEvaluationAstViolation.SingletonSequencePattern`, `MultipleCollectingCaptures`, `RepeatedNameIncludesCollecting`, `IllegalInEval`) anywhere in the tree, a host-built PARENT scope's open targets and properties included (owner decision 2026-10-12: `PreEvaluationValidationWalker.VisitParentScopes`, Lean `validateScopeTree`, `HostBuiltParentScopeValidationTests`, `CoreTests/ParentScopeValidation.lean`; formerly such a scope was never examined). `C1(a, *p)` / `C2(b, *q)` / `K = C1 + C2` is the DEFINITION's `DiagnosticCode.InvalidCollectingBinding` at elaboration (formerly a planner `InvalidOperationException` out of `KatLangEngine.Run`), naming both collectors and their callees; a shared collecting NAME is one binding (`K = while + repeat` is `K(step, *init, count)`); recovery keeps each level's first collector (`KeepFirstCollectingCapturePerLevel`). The OUTPUT rule too (X-07): an algorithm whose completed signature has parameters and no output — written lists are the parser's — is the front end's `ExplicitParametersRequireOutput` after resolution (`InferredParameterOutputValidator`, the evaluator gate's own test), at the first inferred parameter's occurrence, else the definition, else the import site, worded for inferred parameters; never the gate's unpositioned run-time failure. `InferredSignatureValidityTests`, `InferredParameterOutputValidationTests`, the X-02 signature-validity laws (`x02_*`, `two_collectors_at_one_level_are_an_invalid_signature`), `CoreTests/StructuralPatterns.lean` § 10. 63:- `open Name` may target a lexically visible private head, but open-provided names and dotted open steps select PUBLIC members (`NotPublicProperty` otherwise), while structural dot access selects DECLARED members, private included. SELECTION NEVER DEPENDS ON EXPOSURE (K1-08): selection by visibility first, then ONE accessibility check of the unique selected member (`Evaluator.IsAccessibleFrom` / Lean `memberAccessible?`) requiring the declaration AND its activation in the site's lexical chain; capture requirements retain the exact semantic owner through shadowing (`Property.RequiredAncestorParameters`, `CaptureRequirements` / `PropDef.requiredOwnerDepths`, `PendingReference`); declaration tokens distinguish same-named algorithms and clause families, activation tokens distinguish calls — both are FIELDS of the runtime model, never a side table (`Algorithm.Declaration`, minted per constructed `User`/`Conditional` and carried by every record copy, so a `with` copy is a view of the same declaration; `ScopeCtx.Owner`/`Activation`, set only by the evaluator's scope construction paths; `EvalCtx.HeadScope`, cleared by every push). An OPEN PROVIDER needs zero effective call parameters and can be neither a clause family nor a prelude builtin, bare or as the head of a dotted target (`OpenProviderValidator`; `IllegalInOpen`, refused eagerly by the front end and by kind at open resolution); since M4★ OD-C a transparent reference opens its TARGET — judged by the target's own rule, under the target's provider identity — and a carrier, like a runtime reference, opens only its own public declarations, a family exposes no branch members structurally, and classification never invalidates selection, so there is no recheck round. Every open target must RESOLVE — an unknown head (never resolved through another open), a missing, private, or branch-only step — from a name head or an inline block/module head alike — is `DiagnosticCode.UnresolvedOpenTarget` whether or not a lookup consults it, and dependency analysis settles an inline-headed provider at its own open level like the evaluator (PV-11) — and exposure analysis settles an escaping name one open LEVEL at a time: two providers at the deciding level charge NOTHING (the evaluator's `ambiguousOpen`), never the first-listed one. `LocalMemberAccessTests`, `ZeroArgPropertyCacheScopeTests`, `NameResolutionAuditTests`, `CoreTests/NameOwnership.lean`. Inline `{ … }` targets and EVERY loaded module, whatever holds it (Q-31 H-P, bullet below), are rooted at the prelude (they see builtins and host operations, never the opener's names); rooting decides what they SEE, never which front-end rules apply inside them, so a declaration invalid as a property body is invalid there too (constitution MOD-06): the implicit-argument resolver's open-target walk reports into the caller's diagnostic sink like every other region (X-48, resolved October 2026; `OpenTargetResolverValidationTests`). 70:- THE DOT ROUTE (Q-17 S-C, decided October 5 2026): an ordinary non-spread edge `R.n(args?)` resolves in ONE order with ONE property lookup — (1) a DECLARED structural member `n` wins whatever its spelling, `string` included, and accessibility is checked after selection (K1-08); (2) a member declared only in clause branches is `LocalOnlyProperty`; (3) on a structural MISS, `n == string` is the number-to-text intrinsic; (4) otherwise the extension fallback `n(R, args)`. A lexical `string` is never consulted by `.string` (`string(x) = 99` / `3.string` is `'3'`, `string(3)` is 99), and `R*.n(args)` stays `n(R*, args)`. Dot-call uses structural lookup first and lexical fallback second at EVERY level of a chain: an argumentless receiver — a `.string` edge included — is NAVIGATED through its declared structural members before the outer edge is resolved (`resolveDotReceiver` / `ResolveDotReceiver`, the ONE receiver resolution shared by the sync evaluator, the async twin, and the sequence optimizer, mirrored statically by `AstHelpers.ResolveStaticStructuralMemberProvider`, by alias targets, and by the editor; `Obj.string.Q` reads the declared `string` member's `Q`); an intermediate that is inaccessible from the site (K1-08) or declared only in branches is that edge's `LocalOnlyProperty` error; a receiver without the member, an argument-bearing edge, or an intrinsic `.string` is a value, so the chain continues by extension fallback (`3.A.B` is `B(A(3))`); navigation is identity-only and the higher-order channel is untouched. A MISSING MEMBER ON A STATICALLY KNOWN RECEIVER (G-24) falls back lexically like any receiver — a visible lexical callable is a VALID fallback, an unresolved name in an inferring body becomes an implicit parameter, and under a closed list or clause branch the CERTAIN fallback name is checked like a written callee name (Q-75 F-A, the dotted-call bullet below) — and static receiver knowledge never changes RESOLUTION: it serves diagnostics (`ImplicitParameterProvenance.DotMemberOrigin`, member-surface suggestions, member-token positioning) and decides only whether a fallback is certain; no layer branches on the receiver's spelling. A provenance note is ONE shared object per promotion, carried by the inferred capture, its declarations, the causing dot edge (`Expr.DotCall.InferredFallbackProvenance`), every lifted caller, and the error snapshots in an equality-transparent `RuntimeStateSlot<T>` field (the one storage shape for record-carried state, never a side table or a hand-written copy constructor), and mutated only by the post-exposure `DotMemberProvenanceFinalizer` (`ImplicitParameterProvenanceAttachmentTests`). `ChainedDotStructuralPrecedenceTests`, `ReceiverAwareMissingMemberDiagnosticsTests`, the `dot-chain-*` spec cases. 81:## Lean/C# Alignment
83:Before editing, classify the change with `src/KatLang/SEMANTIC-ALIGNMENT.md`; its "Lean update required?" column is authoritative. Observable semantics require Lean consideration and usually Lean updates plus parity tests; C# implementation/tooling-only changes need C# tests only; optimization-only changes leave Lean untouched but need equivalence tests against the generic path; diagnostic wording-only changes need no Lean when the structured error kind/payload is unchanged; grammar or AST changes usually need Lean review; numeric changes route by tier (the numeric bullet below). This decides the required semantic EDITS only — validation scope is decided by the risk level in `Validation`: a C#-only optimizer, async, or ownership change that needs no Lean edit is still V3 when it touches a V3 trigger, so all seven Lean targets run with no `.lean` change, and an unchanged `.lean` file is no evidence that C# is still aligned. When semantics change, update every affected layer in the same task: Lean, C# parser/elaboration/evaluator, `src/KatLang/Semantics/`, tests and the canonical corpus, `KatLang.ebnf`, `tutorial.md`, and the generator guidance.
93:- BOUNDED DIAGNOSTIC LISTS AND SPLICE CHARGING (September 2026; C#-only host policy): `DiagnosticBag` is the ONE accumulator of one diagnostic LIST — a parse (lexer, parser, load guard, module loader with every nested module, every elaboration pass) or one deferred materialization (its own list, in that evaluation's error) — with capacity `SourceProcessingLimits.MaxDiagnosticCount` (default = hard max 1000). PREFIX LAW: the first N diagnostics the unbounded operation would report, in order, then ONE unpositioned `DiagnosticCountExceeded` marker (not counted; most severe dropped severity); a report past N is counted, never constructed or formatted. A report a pass decides LATER (M4★: a check implicit-argument resolution decides) takes the place the deferring pass (parameter detection) reserved for it (`DiagnosticBag.ReserveAnchor` / `InsertingAt`): the list is the one the operation would have produced had the report been made at its anchor, and the prefix law holds for it. Every decision reads the COUNTERS (`ReportedCount`, `ReportedErrorCount`, `HasReported`, the lexer's `lexicalErrorStarts`), never the stored list, so trees, downloads, caching, and gating are identical at any capacity; a withheld list (a provisional elaboration's passes) reports into a `CreateStage()` bag of the same capacity that is never committed. Stored messages are at most 4096 code units, and per-reference echoes of declaration text are bounded where formatted (`ExprNameRenderer.BoundName`/`BoundedJoin`). Every cache-hit module SPLICE charges its elaborated weight against the aggregate (`CachedModule.Weight`; released with a cancelled frame through its `SpliceLedger`). The analyses behind the reports stay linear — one span walk per body (`FindFirstResolveSpans`), one forwarding verdict per callee and region (`MissingForwardingNames`), interned collision contexts (`ContextId`) — each pinned by a traversal observation. `DiagnosticBudgetTests`. 123:## Builtins And Spread Conventions
157:## Editor Semantics
167:## Testing Expectations
172:- Test design, adversarial coverage, failure analysis, and validation execution all belong to the primary agent; a subagent is for a bulky self-contained investigation only, never for running tests (see `Validation`).
178:## Documentation Expectations
183:- In this repo that usually includes `.github/agents/katlang-generator.agent.md` and any related generator prompt assets.

186:## Coding Guidance
195:## Validation
197:Validation scope follows REGRESSION RISK, never line count, file count, or file extension alone. The alignment manifest and the language rules decide which semantic EDITS a change needs (Lean, C#, corpus, docs); this section decides how much local validation the candidate gets and how it is executed. `.github/workflows/validate.yml` stays the full .NET + Lean backstop for pull requests and pushes to `main`: a local V0–V2 omission is a deliberate risk decision, and CI is never a reason to skip V3 locally. It IS the reason a local V1/V2 stays bounded: the backstop catches what a scoped run misses, so a V1/V2 run is never padded with a full phase "to be safe".
199:### Candidate and level
201:- Assess the COMPLETE candidate: the relevant commits plus staged, unstaged, untracked, deleted, and renamed files. A clean working tree is not evidence that a committed candidate needs no tests. Preserve unrelated work and account for it when it affects the candidate or the test results.
202:- Classify by semantic impact, dependency reach, and changed contracts. Start at V1 unless the change is clearly V0, then apply the V2/V3 triggers; when the impact cannot be confidently bounded, choose V3. Record the level and a one-line reason before validation starts; the level may be raised on evidence, never lowered. The level is also the execution plan: V0–V2 run only what their row names, and the full `validate-all.ps1` phases belong to V3 alone — if the candidate warrants a full phase, record V3; running one at V1/V2 is a misclassification, not extra diligence.
204:| Level | Appropriate scope | Required local validation |
209:| V3 — full | Fundamental behavior, broadly shared infrastructure, cross-cutting changes, or uncertain impact | Complete local .NET validation and all seven canonical Lean targets, plus any specifically required regression/parity checks. |
211:V3 is MANDATORY for changes to parser/grammar behavior or AST structure; elaboration; lexical ownership/name resolution; parameter binding or implicit lifting; Grace; sequence/list/spread/collect/arity semantics; the evaluator core; the optimizer/planned execution; sync/async/cancellation behavior; core loading/module semantics; caching/exposure; Decimal128/numeric semantics; Lean/C# correspondence; and widely reused infrastructure or build/toolchain changes with broad impact. The triggers concern the behavior or machinery changed: a comment fix inside `Parser.cs` is not V3, a one-line ownership fix is; a formatting-only string-construction refactor may be V1 when the output contract is demonstrably unchanged; updating expected semantic results never makes a semantic change test-only. V2 covers bounded production-behavior changes, shared consumers, and API/diagnostic contracts without a V3 trigger — an isolated CLI presentation change needs no evaluator-wide validation, a change to shared loading or cancellation does. Executable documentation is not prose: tutorial result claims, spec-linked examples, generated prompt blocks, and the EBNF keep their verification tests (coverage map below) even when only text files changed, so such a change is neither automatically V0 nor V3; changed language MEANING is still V3 plus the semantic-update process.
213:### Lean validation
216:- V1/V2: build the affected Lean targets and the dependent artifact/parity checks whenever Lean code, proofs, guards, imports, or generated Lean content changes or is affected; a meaningful Lean-only change never gets zero Lean validation, and unclear dependency reach means V3. Pure Lean comments may be V0; regenerating an artifact without a content change is not itself a semantic change.
218:### Commands
226:Its .NET phase runs the FULL solution build (every project — `dotnet test` alone builds only test projects and their dependencies, so benchmark/demo compile breaks escape it), then the C# suite with `--no-build`, then `git diff --check`; its Lean phase owns the one canonical seven-target list. The script accepts only `All` (the default), `DotNet`, and `Lean` (plus `-ForceInvocationPlans`, below): it has no focused or level switch and does not detect risk. Completing `-Phase DotNet` and then `-Phase Lean`, one after the other, against the same unchanged candidate satisfies V3 — do not rerun `All` merely to repeat completed work, and never run the two phases side by side — while a partial phase alone is never full validation. A phase already runs every focused suite, so it is never preceded, accompanied, or followed by a separate filtered pass over the same candidate. Each phase fingerprints the staged, unstaged, and untracked state and fails if validation changes it; a checkout may start dirty, but validation must leave it exactly as it started.

199:### Candidate and level
201:- Assess the COMPLETE candidate: the relevant commits plus staged, unstaged, untracked, deleted, and renamed files. A clean working tree is not evidence that a committed candidate needs no tests. Preserve unrelated work and account for it when it affects the candidate or the test results.
202:- Classify by semantic impact, dependency reach, and changed contracts. Start at V1 unless the change is clearly V0, then apply the V2/V3 triggers; when the impact cannot be confidently bounded, choose V3. Record the level and a one-line reason before validation starts; the level may be raised on evidence, never lowered. The level is also the execution plan: V0–V2 run only what their row names, and the full `validate-all.ps1` phases belong to V3 alone — if the candidate warrants a full phase, record V3; running one at V1/V2 is a misclassification, not extra diligence.
204:| Level | Appropriate scope | Required local validation |
209:| V3 — full | Fundamental behavior, broadly shared infrastructure, cross-cutting changes, or uncertain impact | Complete local .NET validation and all seven canonical Lean targets, plus any specifically required regression/parity checks. |
211:V3 is MANDATORY for changes to parser/grammar behavior or AST structure; elaboration; lexical ownership/name resolution; parameter binding or implicit lifting; Grace; sequence/list/spread/collect/arity semantics; the evaluator core; the optimizer/planned execution; sync/async/cancellation behavior; core loading/module semantics; caching/exposure; Decimal128/numeric semantics; Lean/C# correspondence; and widely reused infrastructure or build/toolchain changes with broad impact. ## Testing Expectations

- Prefer minimal, semantics-preserving, reviewable changes.
- Add or update focused tests near the changed layer.
- Include negative coverage when failure modes are meaningful.
- Test design, adversarial coverage, failure analysis, and validation execution all belong to the primary agent; a subagent is for a bulky self-contained investigation only, never for running tests (see `Validation`).
- If a change crosses parser, evaluator, semantics, or docs boundaries, cover the affected layers in the same task when feasible.
- **A source-based evaluator test must PARSE CLEANLY, and must assert the error TYPE, not merely that something failed.** `Parser.Parse(source).Root` silently discards diagnostics, so a test whose source the parser rejects still evaluates the recovery tree and can pass for an unrelated reason — that is how a `NotPublicProperty` regression passed without ever reaching the branch, and how 41 `EvaluatorTests` came to run on illegal source. Use `SourceProvenance.ParseValid(...)` (or `EvaluatorTestSupport.ParseValidRoot`) for ordinary source semantics; `SourceProvenance.ExpectFrontEndError(...)` when the parser/elaborator is the subject; `SourceProvenance.ParseAllowingDiagnostics(...)` only where malformed source is the point (recovery, fuzz, editor tooling). Never assert an evaluator outcome on a source you have not shown to be legal.
- **A strict allocation assertion (exactly zero bytes, an exact count, or two equal counts) is a `*_GcIsolatedChild` test** (`tests/KatLang.Tests/Infrastructure/GcIsolatedAllocation.cs`): during a background GC, `GC.GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread` can report up to one allocation quantum (~8 KB) for an allocation-free window (dotnet/runtime#134724). Such tests therefore run in one child test host per assembly with `DOTNET_gcConcurrent=0`, and the pinned `GcIsolatedAllocationTests` (core) and `CliGcIsolatedAllocationTests` inventories require each to complete there. Coarse bounds and ratios stay in-process; warm up before the window and keep assertions outside it.
- **Before writing a source test for an evaluator branch, check the branch is surface-reachable at all.** Front-end elaboration can make it dead: clause-family elaboration turns every single-clause binder form into an `Algorithm.User`, so the flat-binder arm of `ConditionalValueAccessError` cannot be reached from any written program, and implicit-parameter promotion hides the dotted-`open` visibility checks. A source test for such a branch passes while the branch stays dead — pin these from a prebuilt AST instead (`EvaluatorDefensiveBranchTests`).

## Documentation Expectations

- Update `KatLang.ebnf` when lexer/parser grammar changes. Its identifier/keyword terminal claims are mechanically checked by `EbnfLexicalSyncTests`: changing identifier characters or the keyword set requires updating the lexer, the EBNF, and the independent contract tests together; harmless wrapping and alternative reordering are not policy changes.
- Update `tutorial.md` when user-facing behavior changes.
- Update generator-facing files when syntax, builtins, `open`/`load`, or recommended code-generation idioms change.
- In this repo that usually includes `.github/agents/katlang-generator.agent.md` and any related generator prompt assets.
- When generator guidance changes, explicitly check both `.github/agents/katlang-generator.agent.md` and `experimental/prompts/katlang-generator.txt`.

## Coding Guidance

- Prefer small changes that fix the root semantic issue without widening scope unnecessarily.
- Do not introduce new AST shapes unless strongly justified by Lean or an existing architectural boundary.
- Reuse the owning logic instead of re-encoding the same rule across parser, elaboration, evaluator, or semantic-model code, and preserve the current parser/evaluator/tooling boundaries.
- Keep diagnostics structured, source-positioned, user-friendly, and phrased in KatLang terms.
- If a change is implementation-only optimization, say so explicitly.
- **A `CancellationToken` is always the LAST parameter** — internal and private signatures included, several trailing tokens allowed; a parameter added to a list that ends with a token goes BEFORE it. `CancellationTokenParameterOrderTests` pins this by reflection over the KatLang assembly, and focused runs that left it out let violations survive until V3 repeatedly. Validation scope follows REGRESSION RISK, never line count, file count, or file extension alone. - Classify by semantic impact, dependency reach, and changed contracts. Start at V1 unless the change is clearly V0, then apply the V2/V3 triggers; when the impact cannot be confidently bounded, choose V3. Record the level and a one-line reason before validation starts; the level may be raised on evidence, never lowered. The level is also the execution plan: V0–V2 run only what their row names, and the full `validate-all.ps1` phases belong to V3 alone — if the candidate warrants a full phase, record V3; running one at V1/V2 is a misclassification, not extra diligence.
