## Testing Expectations

- Prefer minimal, semantics-preserving, reviewable changes.
- Add or update focused tests near the changed layer.
- Include negative coverage when failure modes are meaningful.
- Test design, adversarial coverage, failure analysis, and validation execution all belong to the primary agent; a subagent is for a bulky self-contained investigation only, never for running tests (see `Validation`).
- If a change crosses parser, evaluator, semantics, or docs boundaries, cover the affected layers in the same task when feasible.
- **A source-based evaluator test must PARSE CLEANLY, and must assert the error TYPE, not merely that something failed.** `Parser.Parse(source).Root` silently discards diagnostics, so a test whose source the parser rejects still evaluates the recovery tree and can pass for an unrelated reason — that is how a `NotPublicProperty` regression passed without ever reaching the branch, and how 41 `EvaluatorTests` came to run on illegal source. Use `SourceProvenance.ParseValid(...)` (or `EvaluatorTestSupport.ParseValidRoot`) for ordinary source semantics; `SourceProvenance.ExpectFrontEndError(...)` when the parser/elaborator is the subject; `SourceProvenance.ParseAllowingDiagnostics(...)` only where malformed source is the point (recovery, fuzz, editor tooling). Never assert an evaluator outcome on a source you have not shown to be legal.
- **A strict allocation assertion (exactly zero bytes, an exact count, or two equal counts) is a `*_GcIsolatedChild` test** (`tests/KatLang.Tests/Infrastructure/GcIsolatedAllocation.cs`): during a background GC, `GC.GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread` can report up to one allocation quantum (~8 KB) for an allocation-free window (dotnet/runtime#134724). Such tests therefore run in one child test host per assembly with `DOTNET_gcConcurrent=0`, and the pinned `GcIsolatedAllocationTests` (core) and `CliGcIsolatedAllocationTests` inventories require each to complete there. Coarse bounds and ratios stay in-process; warm up before the window and keep assertions outside it.
- **Before writing a source test for an evaluator branch, check the branch is surface-reachable at all.** Front-end elaboration can make it dead: clause-family elaboration turns every single-clause binder form into an `Algorithm.User`, so the flat-binder arm of `ConditionalValueAccessError` cannot be reached from any written program, and implicit-parameter promotion hides the dotted-`open` visibility checks. A source test for such a branch passes while the branch stays dead — pin these from a prebuilt AST instead (`EvaluatorDefensiveBranchTests`).

## Documentation Expectations

- Update `KatLang.ebnf` when lexer/parser grammar changes. Its identifier/keyword terminal claims are mechanically checked by `EbnfLexicalSyncTests`: changing identifier characters or the keyword set requires updating the lexer, the EBNF, and the independent contract tests together; harmless wrapping and alternative reordering are not policy changes.
- Update `tutorial.md` when user-facing behavior changes.
- Update generator-facing files when syntax, builtins, `open`/`load`, or recommended code-generation idioms change.
- In this repo that usually includes `.github/agents/katlang-generator.agent.md` and any related generator prompt assets.
- When generator guidance changes, explicitly check both `.github/agents/katlang-generator.agent.md` and `experimental/prompts/katlang-generator.txt`.

## Coding Guidance

- Prefer small changes that fix the root semantic issue without widening scope unnecessarily.
- Do not introduce new AST shapes unless strongly justified by Lean or an existing architectural boundary.
- Reuse the owning logic instead of re-encoding the same rule across parser, elaboration, evaluator, or semantic-model code, and preserve the current parser/evaluator/tooling boundaries.
- Keep diagnostics structured, source-positioned, user-friendly, and phrased in KatLang terms.
- If a change is implementation-only optimization, say so explicitly.
- **A `CancellationToken` is always the LAST parameter** — internal and private signatures included, several trailing tokens allowed; a parameter added to a list that ends with a token goes BEFORE it. `CancellationTokenParameterOrderTests` pins this by reflection over the KatLang assembly, and focused runs that left it out let violations survive until V3 repeatedly. After ANY C# method or constructor signature change (evaluator, `NeedCell`, async, runtime, loader, host operations), run `pwsh -NoProfile -File ./scripts/check-cancellation-token-order.ps1` as the first focused check, before feature tests and V3: it builds the test project from the current sources, runs the whole class, prints every violating signature, and exits nonzero on a violation, a build failure, or a filter that executes nothing.

## Validation

Validation scope follows REGRESSION RISK, never line count, file count, or file extension alone. The alignment manifest and the language rules decide which semantic EDITS a change needs (Lean, C#, corpus, docs); this section decides how much local validation the candidate gets and how it is executed. `.github/workflows/validate.yml` stays the full .NET + Lean backstop for pull requests and pushes to `main`: a local V0–V2 omission is a deliberate risk decision, and CI is never a reason to skip V3 locally. It IS the reason a local V1/V2 stays bounded: the backstop catches what a scoped run misses, so a V1/V2 run is never padded with a full phase "to be safe".

### Candidate and level

- Assess the COMPLETE candidate: the relevant commits plus staged, unstaged, untracked, deleted, and renamed files. A clean working tree is not evidence that a committed candidate needs no tests. Preserve unrelated work and account for it when it affects the candidate or the test results.
- Classify by semantic impact, dependency reach, and changed contracts. Start at V1 unless the change is clearly V0, then apply the V2/V3 triggers; when the impact cannot be confidently bounded, choose V3. Record the level and a one-line reason before validation starts; the level may be raised on evidence, never lowered. The level is also the execution plan: V0–V2 run only what their row names, and the full `validate-all.ps1` phases belong to V3 alone — if the candidate warrants a full phase, record V3; running one at V1/V2 is a misclassification, not extra diligence.

| Level | Appropriate scope | Required local validation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| V0 — trivial | Instruction/prose edits, comments, or formatting proven not to affect execution or mechanically checked content | Review the diff, whitespace (`git diff --check`), and the references/consistency of the text. No build or runtime suite for a genuinely documentation-only change. |
| V1 — focused | Small, isolated, behavior-preserving refactor or test change with a well-understood dependency boundary | Build the affected project/test dependency closure; run the directly related tests with verified filters. |
| V2 — affected | Bounded subsystem behavior change; a limited shared helper, API, or diagnostic contract change; neighboring consumers affected | Focused tests plus the neighboring/affected suites, the affected project builds, and the applicable parity/artifact/Lean checks — never the full solution suite or a `validate-all.ps1` phase. |
| V3 — full | Fundamental behavior, broadly shared infrastructure, cross-cutting changes, or uncertain impact | Complete local .NET validation and all seven canonical Lean targets, plus any specifically required regression/parity checks. |

V3 is MANDATORY for changes to parser/grammar behavior or AST structure; elaboration; lexical ownership/name resolution; parameter binding or implicit lifting; Grace; sequence/list/spread/collect/arity semantics; the evaluator core; the optimizer/planned execution; sync/async/cancellation behavior; core loading/module semantics; caching/exposure; Decimal128/numeric semantics; Lean/C# correspondence; and widely reused infrastructure or build/toolchain changes with broad impact. The triggers concern the behavior or machinery changed: a comment fix inside `Parser.cs` is not V3, a one-line ownership fix is; a formatting-only string-construction refactor may be V1 when the output contract is demonstrably unchanged; updating expected semantic results never makes a semantic change test-only. V2 covers bounded production-behavior changes, shared consumers, and API/diagnostic contracts without a V3 trigger — an isolated CLI presentation change needs no evaluator-wide validation, a change to shared loading or cancellation does. Executable documentation is not prose: tutorial result claims, spec-linked examples, generated prompt blocks, and the EBNF keep their verification tests (coverage map below) even when only text files changed, so such a change is neither automatically V0 nor V3; changed language MEANING is still V3 plus the semantic-update process.

### Lean validation

- V3 always runs all seven Lean targets, even when no `.lean` file changed — a C#-only optimizer, async, or ownership change is V3, and `SemanticExplorerCases`/`LanguageSpecCases` are how Lean/C# correspondence is checked.
- V1/V2: build the affected Lean targets and the dependent artifact/parity checks whenever Lean code, proofs, guards, imports, or generated Lean content changes or is affected; a meaningful Lean-only change never gets zero Lean validation, and unclear dependency reach means V3. Pure Lean comments may be V0; regenerating an artifact without a content change is not itself a semantic change.

### Commands

The normal V3 command, from the repo root:

```powershell
pwsh -NoProfile -File ./scripts/validate-all.ps1 -Phase All
```

Its .NET phase runs the FULL solution build (every project — `dotnet test` alone builds only test projects and their dependencies, so benchmark/demo compile breaks escape it), then the C# suite with `--no-build`, then `git diff --check`; its Lean phase owns the one canonical seven-target list. The script accepts only `All` (the default), `DotNet`, and `Lean` (plus `-ForceInvocationPlans`, below): it has no focused or level switch and does not detect risk. Completing `-Phase DotNet` and then `-Phase Lean`, one after the other, against the same unchanged candidate satisfies V3 — do not rerun `All` merely to repeat completed work, and never run the two phases side by side — while a partial phase alone is never full validation. A phase already runs every focused suite, so it is never preceded, accompanied, or followed by a separate filtered pass over the same candidate. Each phase fingerprints the staged, unstaged, and untracked state and fails if validation changes it; a checkout may start dirty, but validation must leave it exactly as it started.

FORCED INVOCATION-PLAN RUN: `pwsh -NoProfile -File ./scripts/validate-all.ps1 -Phase DotNet -ForceInvocationPlans` runs the same .NET phase with `KATLANG_FORCE_INVOCATION_PLANS=1` set before any test host starts (`ForcedInvocationPlansHook`, read once at test-assembly load), so every evaluator run of `KatLang.Tests` retains invocation plans and every call-shaped supplied argument takes the plan route; the ordinary phase REMOVES an inherited flag. It is a different execution mode, not a repeated pass, and it must pass in full: a change to invocation plans, call references/META, the J7 plan-retention gate, or supplied-cell/need binding runs it after its V3 `-Phase DotNet`. A route-dependent expectation (plan/supply-formation counts, `RetainsInvocationPlans`, plan-disabled fusion hits) selects between its two independently justified expectations with `ForcedInvocationPlansHook.Forced`; values, effects, charges and diagnostics never depend on the mode. Manual equivalent: set or remove the variable in the CHILD process environment, never with `Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable` inside a test.

Manual .NET fallback (equivalent, including the independent full-solution build):

```powershell
dotnet build .\KatLang.slnx -p:UseSharedCompilation=false
dotnet test .\KatLang.slnx -p:UseSharedCompilation=false --no-build
git diff --check
```

Manual Lean fallback (all seven targets — V3, or a V1/V2 change that affects Lean):

### Execution discipline

Validation is executed by the primary agent, in ONE execution stream: never two of `dotnet build`, `dotnet test`, `lake build`, a `validate-all.ps1` phase, or a regeneration run in flight at once — concurrent `dotnet test` invocations lock `KatLang.Tests.dll` (MSB3027), a phase fingerprints the tree while it runs, and a second run of the same suite over an unchanged candidate is pure duplication. Every command's full output goes to a log file (the ignored `artifacts/validation/` directory or a temporary directory) and only its summary lines — result totals, failure identities, exit code — are read back, never the whole log.

- ONE plan per candidate, chosen before anything runs: at V1/V2 the focused and affected suites, most informative first, and nothing beyond them; at V3 the full phases only. Development checks while editing stay minimal — the test class being written, `scripts/check-cancellation-token-order.ps1` after a signature change (`Coding Guidance`), the one previously failing check after a repair, the Lean target that compiles the edited file, a regeneration run — because the plan runs everything else exactly once; a pre-validation sweep of neighboring suites runs every test twice.
- One command at a time, waited to completion: a `--no-build` run only after the build's exit code is in hand, `lake build` never beside a `dotnet` command, the .NET phase and then the Lean phase, never side by side. A `validate-all.ps1` phase exceeds the foreground time limit, so run it as ONE background command and then wait for its completion — no polling loop (every poll re-reads the whole context), no other command, and no edit to the checkout until it has finished.
- On a failure, capture the command, the failure identity, and the evidence; decide what it means; repair; rerun only the failing check; then complete the plan for the FINAL candidate. Reuse earlier results only while their inputs, dependencies, configuration, and environment still apply (later prose-only edits do not by themselves invalidate runtime results). When a failure suggests wider regression, or the diff reveals a V3 trigger the classification missed, raise the scope one level at a time — never as a precaution — and a full phase replaces the remaining focused plan instead of adding to it. Do not rerun an unchanged failure repeatedly, and do not launch every suite to diagnose a missing SDK.
- Never claim validation from a partial run, a stale build, an unexecuted command, a zero-test filter, or an assumption that CI will pass, and do not label a failure pre-existing or flaky without evidence. Report what ran, the counts, the failures, what was omitted and why, and the log paths.

### Subagents

Do not delegate test execution. Measured in September 2026, a validation worker spent 30–50 requests to run two or three commands — about ten times the cost of running them inline — could not work in parallel with a tree that must stay frozen, and shared no prompt cache with the primary agent (caches are model-scoped and prefix-exact). A subagent is for a BULKY, SELF-CONTAINED INVESTIGATION whose intermediate reading would otherwise flood the primary context — a failure hunt across many files, an inventory, a cross-file audit. Give it the cheapest model that can do the job, a bounded brief with an explicit stopping point, and ask for `file:line` facts; code the primary agent will edit or reason about it reads itself, in bounded ranges. Never spawn one for a single known file, and never let one edit, regenerate, or validate.

### Subsystem coverage map

Guides focused V1/V2 execution and supplements the level table; it never weakens a V3 requirement.

- Parser/syntax: `LexerTests`, `ParserTests`, `ParserDiagnosticSpanTests`, `ParserDiagnosticWordingTests`, `SameLineSeparatorTests`, `StarSyntaxTests`, `MarkerAttachmentTests`, `DeclarationHeadLineRuleTests`, `RootStrayCloserRecoveryTests`, `GroupedExpressionSpanTests`, the relevant editor span tests, `LanguageSpecRunnerTests`, `LeanAstEncoderTests`, the STR-02 `Interpolation/InterpolationLexerTests` and `InterpolationSyntaxTests`, and the Lean `AstDemo`/`CoreTests`/`LanguageSpecCases` guards.
- Ownership/binding/evaluator: the `Evaluator*Tests` families, `ParameterOwnershipTests`, `StaticOpenOwnershipTests`, `OwnershipConformanceTests`, `LookupCoherenceTests`, `LookupTwinEquivalenceTests`, `CompletionIdentityDifferentialTests`, `ParameterDetectorTests`, `ImplicitArgumentResolverTests`, `CountedMatrixTests` (plain/counted results), `CorpusExecutionEquivalenceTests` (generic/planned), `AsyncTwinDifferentialTests` (forced async) where applicable, the STR-02 `Interpolation/*Tests` (semantics, demand, limits, front end, host AST), `LanguageSpecRunnerTests`, `SemanticExplorerTests`, and the Lean `CoreTests`/`SemanticExplorerCases`/`LanguageSpecCases` correspondence.
- Optimizer: `LoopStrategyPreparationTests`, `EvaluatorLoopTests`, the `LoopPlanned*ParityTests`, `EvaluatorSequencePipelineTests`, `SequencePipelineDispatchTests`, `SequencePreparationParityTests`, `FilterCountFusionSpanParityTests`, `OptimizerEquivalenceSweepTests`, `CountedDispatchChargingTests`, `OperationalMetamorphicTests` (operational counters/diagnostics), `AsyncTwinDifferentialTests`, and — when the change warrants it — `StructuralFuzzTests`/`MetamorphicFuzzHarnessTests`. Establish that the selected tests exercise the intended execution path (planned versus generic).
- Editor-only tooling: `SemanticModelTests`, `SemanticModelDeclarationRegistrationTests`, `CompletionIdentityDifferentialTests`, `MathAliasSemanticModelTests`, `EditorReadinessTests`, `EditorFuzzHarnessTests`; escalate when shared elaboration or ownership is involved.
- CLI/API/rendering: `tests/KatLang.CLI.Tests`, `tests/KatLang.Formatting.PublicApi.Tests` (`PublicApiBaselineTests`, `PublicElaborationSurfaceTests`, `PublicFormatterExtensionTests`), the `Formatting/*` tests, `KatLangEngineTests`, `Hosting/*`, `AsyncEvaluationApiTests`, and direct consumers; widen when shared runtime behavior changes.
- Executable documentation/artifacts: `TutorialSpecTests`, `TutorialResultSweepTests`, `TutorialCorpusParserTests`, `LanguageSpecArtifactsTests` and `LanguageSpecArtifactsGeneratorPromptTests` (both match `--filter LanguageSpecArtifacts`), `SemanticExplorerLeanArtifactTests`, `HostParentDifferentialTests`, `EbnfLexicalSyncTests`, `PublicApiBaselineTests`, `ArtifactRegenerationPolicyTests`, `ReleaseVersionSourceTests`, and `ContinuousIntegrationPolicyTests` — verification only; regeneration stays a separate step.

A V3 run is not release publishing, a benchmark campaign, or unbounded fuzzing; additional expensive workloads need a concrete risk or an explicit task requirement.

## Continuous Integration And Releases

- `.github/workflows/validate.yml` is automatic for pull requests and pushes to
  `main`, and can also be dispatched manually. Its stable required-check names
  are `.NET validation` and `Lean validation`; both invoke the phase boundary
  above rather than duplicating commands in YAML. It runs BOTH phases on every
  such event regardless of which files changed — the full .NET + Lean backstop
  behind the risk-based local levels in `Validation` — and it never substitutes
  for a locally required V3.
- `validate-all.ps1` writes a command/exit-code/environment record, one TRX per
  test project, a failure summary and the GC-isolated allocation logs to a fresh
  git-ignored `artifacts/validation/validate-all-*` directory (a temporary
  directory if that path is not ignored). `validate.yml` uploads it with
  `if: always()`; the job result remains the validation result.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` is manual-only. Dispatch it from `main` with
  the version already present in `KatLangVersion.props`. A push, merge, or tag
  never publishes a release automatically.
- The release workflow validates the exact dispatched commit, builds and runs
  the NativeAOT CLI on native Windows/Linux/macOS x64 and ARM64 runners,
  packages the tested executable with the root `LICENSE`, `NOTICE`, and
  `PATENTS` files plus the exact restored RID-specific .NET runtime pack's MIT

- `KatLangVersion.props` remains authoritative. Workflow code must never pass
  an MSBuild version override, create/move an existing version tag, or replace
  an existing release.
- Normal jobs have `contents: read`. Only the final publication job has
  `contents: write`; workflows use no user-managed secrets. External actions
  are pinned to immutable commit SHAs and `.github/dependabot.yml` proposes
  reviewable GitHub Actions pin updates.



"}}

## F1: deterministic finite admission

The old default was max(1,024, GC-reported available memory / 4) accounting bytes. Thus 128-MiB,
256-MiB and 512-MiB GC heaps implicitly selected 32/64/128-MiB envelopes, 32,768/65,536/131,072
entry ceilings and 524,288/1,048,576/2,097,152 metadata slots. The new default is a fixed 1 GiB:
1,048,576 entries and 16,777,216 64-byte ledger slots, subject to tighter operation-scaled bounds.
No admission code reads machine/GC memory.

The explicit additive policy is `SourceProcessingLimits.MaxSupportedStaticStructureBytes` (1 GiB)
and nullable `MaxStaticStructureBytes`. Positive requests below the ceiling lower it; larger requests
clamp; null uses the ceiling. The immutable policy flows through parser/engine, eager modules and
deferred compilation. The additive host-analysis overload is
`SemanticModelBuilder.Build(Algorithm, SourceProcessingLimits, CancellationToken = REDACTED
No global mutable policy is introduced. Already completed exact facts can be reused without admission.

For F = distinct admitted nodes + enumerated edges, the existing operation-scaled work/read limits
remain 16,384 + 1,024F and 65,536 + 4,096F, with four refinements; entries are capped by both
4,096 + 128F and envelope/1,024. Source nodes and edges are bounded by envelope/32 and envelope/8.
Products clamp before multiplication; the fixed ceiling also bounds the source census. The ledger
continues charging entries, subscriptions, callback graphs, temporary sets and adapter/publication
metadata. These conservative accounting units are not a claim about total process bytes.

Sizing retains the established 1-KiB entry and 64-byte slot policy. A 1-GiB fixed envelope provides
substantial room above the original 1,000/2,000-property witnesses, while preserving independent
operation-scaled work safeguards and allowing tighter host policies. Measured allocations and exact
before/after low-memory outcomes are recorded in the evidence below.

The actual 1,000/2,000-property operation uses 33,083/66,083 query entries and
365,339/727,339 peak ledger slots. The complete measured compilation allocates
71,495,048/144,101,160 bytes on the calling thread. The 1-GiB ceiling provides substantial
headroom above these measured families while retaining all operation-scaled work limits;
these allocations include transient compiler work and are not resident-entry byte estimates.
The original two admission controls retain exactly their prior effective 256-MiB and 1-MiB
envelopes after translating from simulated available-memory inputs to explicit policy.

ENV = os.environ.copy()
ENV['GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS'] = '0'

def io(p):
    s = str(Path(p).resolve())
    return Path(s if s.startswith('\\\\?\\') else '\\\\?\\' + s)

def digest(b): return hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()
def sha(p): return digest(io(p).read_bytes())
def read(p): return json.loads(io(p).read_text(encoding='utf-8-sig'))
def dump(n, x): (OUT/n).write_text(json.dumps(x, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding='utf-8')
def git(root, *args):
    r = subprocess.run(['git', '--no-optional-locks', *args], cwd=root, env=ENV, capture_output=True)
    if r.returncode: raise RuntimeError(str(args) + ': ' + r.stderr.decode(errors='replace'))
    return r.stdout

def manifest(base, p):
    rows = {}
    for line in io(p).read_text(encoding='utf-8-sig').splitlines():
        value, name = line.split(' ', 1)
        name = name.lstrip(' *')
        assert sha(base/name) == value, str(base/name)
        rows[name] = value
    return rows

    names = git(root,'ls-files','-z','--cached','--others','--exclude-standard').decode().split('\0')
    r = dict(files={n:sha(root/n) for n in names if n and io(root/n).is_file()},

entire session attach — Attach an existing agent session
Attach an existing agent session that wasn't captured by hooks.

This creates a checkpoint from the session's transcript and links it to the
last commit, or to the commit named by --commit. Use this when hooks failed
to fire or weren't installed when the session started, or to attach a
research session.

How the session is linked follows from two facts about the commit — does it
already have a checkpoint, and is it pushed — the same for HEAD and --commit:
  - It already has a checkpoint: the session is added to it. Git history is
    not changed.
  - It is already pushed: the commit is left unchanged and the link is
    recorded in a new checkpoint, which is pushed right away. The link counts
    once the commit's author attaches it, and names that exact commit: after
    a rebase or amend, attach the session to the new commit.
  - It isn't pushed: the Entire-Checkpoint trailer is added to it, which
    rewrites it and any commits after it on the current branch (their content
    is unchanged). A trailer survives a later rebase. Merges after the commit,
    or a rebase or merge in progress, are refused. If a remote can't be
    reached to confirm the commit isn't pushed, attach refuses rather than
    risk rewriting a shared commit.

attach prints what it is about to do and asks before doing it. Without a
terminal (an agent or a script) it changes nothing and exits non-zero; show
the user what it printed, and once they agree, rerun with --force.

A session can be attached to more than one commit. Each checkpoint records the
turns since the session's previous checkpoint.

Use --review to tag the attached session as an agent review. The
first user prompt in the transcript is recorded as the review prompt.
Pass --skills to declare which skills were actually run; omit to
attach a review without a declared skills list.

Works with any registered agent, including external agents enabled via
external_agents in .entire/settings.local.json (that file only, and only
when it is untracked). Run 'entire agent list' to see the full list.

If --agent doesn't locate a transcript, Entire auto-detects the agent from
the transcript and prints the detected agent name.

When to use this:
Commits made during a session are linked to it automatically. Use this
only when one was missed: `entire session attach <session-id> --commit <sha>`
(default HEAD). Run it without --force first: it prints what it would do

Validation is executed by the primary agent, in ONE execution stream: never two of `dotnet build`, `dotnet test`, `lake build`, a `validate-all.ps1` phase, or a regeneration run in flight at once — concurrent `dotnet test` invocations lock `KatLang.Tests.dll` (MSB3027), a phase fingerprints the tree while it runs, and a second run of the same suite over an unchanged candidate is pure duplication. Every command's full output goes to a log file (the ignored `artifacts/validation/` directory or a temporary directory) and only its summary lines — result totals, failure identities, exit code — are read back, never the whole log.

- ONE plan per candidate, chosen before anything runs: at V1/V2 the focused and affected suites, most informative first, and nothing beyond them; at V3 the full phases only. Development checks while editing stay minimal — the test class being written, `scripts/check-cancellation-token-order.ps1` after a signature change (`Coding Guidance`), the one previously failing check after a repair, the Lean target that compiles the edited file, a regeneration run — because the plan runs everything else exactly once; a pre-validation sweep of neighboring suites runs every test twice.
- One command at a time, waited to completion: a `--no-build` run only after the build's exit code is in hand, `lake build` never beside a `dotnet` command, the .NET phase and then the Lean phase, never side by side. A `validate-all.ps1` phase exceeds the foreground time limit, so run it as ONE background command and then wait for its completion — no polling loop (every poll re-reads the whole context), no other command, and no edit to the checkout until it has finished.
- On a failure, capture the command, the failure identity, and the evidence; decide what it means; repair; rerun only the failing check; then complete the plan for the FINAL candidate. Reuse earlier results only while their inputs, dependencies, configuration, and environment still apply (later prose-only edits do not by themselves invalidate runtime results). When a failure suggests wider regression, or the diff reveals a V3 trigger the classification missed, raise the scope one level at a time — never as a precaution — and a full phase replaces the remaining focused plan instead of adding to it. Do not rerun an unchanged failure repeatedly, and do not launch every suite to diagnose a missing SDK.
- Never claim validation from a partial run, a stale build, an unexecuted command, a zero-test filter, or an assumption that CI will pass, and do not label a failure pre-existing or flaky without evidence. Report what ran, the counts, the failures, what was omitted and why, and the log paths.

### Subagents

Do not delegate test execution. Measured in September 2026, a validation worker spent 30–50 requests to run two or three commands — about ten times the cost of running them inline — could not work in parallel with a tree that must stay frozen, and shared no prompt cache with the primary agent (caches are model-scoped and prefix-exact). A subagent is for a BULKY, SELF-CONTAINED INVESTIGATION whose intermediate reading would otherwise flood the primary context — a failure hunt across many files, an inventory, a cross-file audit. Give it the cheapest model that can do the job, a bounded brief with an explicit stopping point, and ask for `file:line` facts; code the primary agent will edit or reason about it reads itself, in bounded ranges. Never spawn one for a single known file, and never let one edit, regenerate, or validate.

- One command at a time, waited to completion: a `--no-build` run only after the build's exit code is in hand, `lake build` never beside a `dotnet` command, the .NET phase and then the Lean phase, never side by side. A `validate-all.ps1` phase exceeds the foreground time limit, so run it as ONE background command and then wait for its completion — no polling loop (every poll re-reads the whole context), no other command, and no edit to the checkout until it has finished.
- On a failure, capture the command, the failure identity, and the evidence; decide what it means; repair; rerun only the failing check; then complete the plan for the FINAL candidate. Reuse earlier results only while their inputs, dependencies, configuration, and environment still apply (later prose-only edits do not by themselves invalidate runtime results). When a failure suggests wider regression, or the diff reveals a V3 trigger the classification missed, raise the scope one level at a time — never as a precaution — and a full phase replaces the remaining focused plan instead of adding to it. Do not rerun an unchanged failure repeatedly, and do not launch every suite to diagnose a missing SDK.

### Subagents

Do not delegate test execution. Measured in September 2026, a validation worker spent 30–50 requests to run two or three commands — about ten times the cost of running them inline — could not work in parallel with a tree that must stay frozen, and shared no prompt cache with the primary agent (caches are model-scoped and prefix-exact). A subagent is for a BULKY, SELF-CONTAINED INVESTIGATION whose intermediate reading would otherwise flood the primary context — a failure hunt across many files, an inventory, a cross-file audit. Give it the cheapest model that can do the job, a bounded brief with an explicit stopping point, and ask for `file:line` facts; code the primary agent will edit or reason about it reads itself, in bounded ranges. import sys
from pathlib import Path

from support import *

def execute_tests(label,project,expected,mode,filter=None):
    receipt=run(label,test_command(project,label,filter),mode,check=False)
    path=OUT/(label+'.trx')
    if path.exists():audit,keys=parse_trx(path,expected)
    else:audit=dict(expected=len(expected),executed=0,exact_identities=False,all_passed=False,completed=False,missing_trx=True);keys=collections.Counter()
    supervisor=read(OUT/(label+'-supervisor.json'))
    audit.update(exit=receipt['exit'],seconds=receipt['seconds'],mode=mode,source_unchanged=receipt['unchanged'],supervisor=supervisor)
    dump(label+'-audit.json',audit)
    passed=receipt['exit']==0 and supervisor['stop'] is None and audit['completed'] and audit['exact_identities'] and audit['all_passed']
    print('COVERAGE '+label+' '+str(audit['executed'])+'/'+str(len(expected))+' exact='+str(audit['exact_identities'])+' PASS='+str(passed),flush=True)
    return passed,audit,keys

    result={}

        passed,audit,keys=execute_tests('lf-focused-'+mode,'KatLang.Tests',expected,mode,filter)
        result[mode]=audit;dump('focused-acceptance.json',result)
        assert passed,'Focused LF failure: STOP before full-suite execution'
    print('FOCUSED ACCEPTANCE PASS in both modes; exact '+str(len(expected))+' cases per mode.',flush=True)

def complete_mode(mode):
    expected=read(OUT/'expected.json')
    label='lf-canonical-core-'+mode
    passed,audit,coverage=execute_tests(label,'KatLang.Tests',expected,mode)
    result=dict(canonical=audit,batches=[],cli=None,api=None)
    dump(mode+'-runtime-acceptance.json',result)
    if not passed:
        supervisor=audit['supervisor']
        eligible=supervisor['stop'] is not None and supervisor['stop']['reason']=='validation exceeded 15 minutes' and supervisor['counts']['fail_lines']==0
        text=(OUT/(label+'.log')).read_text(encoding='utf-8',errors='replace')
        assert eligible and not any(marker in text for marker in ['[FAIL]','Failed!','[SKIP]','[ERROR]','Unhandled exception']), 'Canonical failure is not eligible for fallback; STOP'
        if not audit.get('missing_trx'):
            assert not audit.get('failures') and all(int(audit['counters'].get(k,0))==0 for k in ['failed','error','notRunnable']), 'Unresolved canonical failures'
        print('CANONICAL '+mode+' INCOMPLETE: correctness-free 900-second timeout; approved fallback now eligible.',flush=True)
        coverage=collections.Counter()
        manifest=read(OUT/'batches/manifest.json')

            filter=(OUT/'batches'/(plan['label']+'-filter.txt')).read_text()
            ok,part,got=execute_tests(name,'KatLang.Tests',rows,mode,filter)
            result['batches'].append(dict(label=name,passed=ok,audit_file=name+'-audit.json',cases=part['executed']))
            dump(mode+'-runtime-acceptance.json',result)

            assert not coverage.keys()&got.keys(),'Duplicate case identity across batches'
            coverage.update(got)
            print('BATCH '+mode+' '+str(index)+'/44 passed; '+str(sum(coverage.values()))+' exact core cases.',flush=True)
    want=collections.Counter((r.get('native_id',r.get('native_parent_id')),r['display']) for r in expected)
    assert coverage==want and len(coverage)==sum(coverage.values())==42333
    result.update(core_passed=42333,core_exact_coverage=True,core_key_digest=hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(sorted((a,b,n) for (a,b),n in coverage.items())).encode()).hexdigest())
    passed,cli,_=execute_tests('lf-cli-'+mode,'KatLang.CLI.Tests',read(OUT/'KatLang.CLI.Tests-inventory/expected.json'),mode)
    result['cli']=cli;dump(mode+'-runtime-acceptance.json',result)
    assert passed,'CLI failure; STOP'

    if mode=='ordinary':
        receipt=read(EXEC/'integration-public-api.json');assert receipt['exit']==0 and receipt['source_index_unchanged']

text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: C:/Users/mikus/.codex/artifacts/b32-lf-integration-validation-20261030/acceptance_audit.py
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+sys.path.insert(0,str(Path(__file__).parent))
+from support import *
+
+assert not (OUT/'lf-v3-acceptance.json').exists()
+frozen()
+expected=read(OUT/'expected.json')
+want=collections.Counter((r.get('native_id',r.get('native_parent_id')),r['display']) for r in expected)
+assert len(want)==sum(want.values())==42333
+discovery=read(OUT/'discovery-inventory-ordinary.json')
+assert len(discovery['cases'])==41778 and discovery['deferred_theories']==19 and len(discovery['expanded_rows'])==574
+assert discovery['cases']==read(OUT/'discovery-inventory-forced.json')['cases']
+assert discovery['expanded_rows']==read(OUT/'discovery-inventory-forced.json')['expanded_rows']
+native=read(OUT/'vstest-inventory.json')
+assert len(native)==len({r['Id'] for r in native})==41778
+manifest=read(OUT/'batches/manifest.json');assert len(manifest['plans'])==44
+classes=collections.Counter(c for p in manifest['plans'] for c in p['classes'])
+collections_seen=[c for p in manifest['plans'] for c in p['collections']]
+assert len(classes)==542 and set(classes.values())=={1}
+assert len(collections_seen)==len(set(collections_seen))==542
+assert set(classes)=={r['Class'] for r in discovery['cases']}
+headers={(r['Class']+'.'+r['Method'],r['Display']) for r in discovery['cases'] if 'TheoryTestCase' in r['Kind']}
+header_ids={r['Id'] for r in native if (r['Fqn'],r['Display']) in headers};assert len(header_ids)==19
+result=dict(status='PASS — exact LF candidate, owner-approved bounded V3',head_before_commits=i.BASE,
+    candidate_tree=read(OUT/'preflight.json')['tree'],core_assembly_sha256=sha(ROOT/'tests/KatLang.Tests/bin/Debug/net11.0/KatLang.Tests.dll'),
+    production_assembly_sha256=sha(ROOT/'src/KatLang/bin/Debug/net11.0/KatLang.dll'),
+    source_entries=1502,collections=542,batches_per_mode=44,static_native_cases=41778,deferred_headers=19,deferred_rows=574,
+    focused={},modes={},reused={},source_unchanged=True,no_correctness_failure=True)
+all_keys={}
+focus=read(OUT/'focused-expected.json')
+assert len(focus)==467 and len(read(OUT/'changed-method-map.json')['methods'])==153
+assert len(read(OUT/'changed-method-map.json')['classes'])==8
+for mode in ['ordinary','forced']:
+    label='lf-focused-'+mode
+    audit,_=parse_trx(OUT/(label+'.trx'),focus)
+    receipt=read(OUT/(label+'.json'))
+    assert receipt['exit']==0 and receipt['mode']==mode and receipt['before']==receipt['after']==read(OUT/'frozen-state.json')

+from pathlib import Path

+def text(root,*args):return git(root,*args).decode().strip()

+    names={n for n in git(root,'ls-files','-z','--cached','--others','--exclude-standard').decode().split('\0') if n}

+def state(root,report=False):

+def metadata(root):
+    result={}
+    for n in ['index','HEAD','config','config.worktree','hooks/pre-commit','hooks/prepare-commit-msg','hooks/commit-msg','hooks/post-commit','hooks/pre-push']:

+    values=p.stdout.decode().splitlines();assert len(values)==len(names)
+    return dict(zip(names,values))
+def safe_no_operations(root):
+    for n in ['MERGE_HEAD','CHERRY_PICK_HEAD','REVERT_HEAD','rebase-merge','rebase-apply','sequencer']:
+        assert not os.path.lexists(text(root,'rev-parse','--path-format=absolute','--git-path',n)),n
+def snapshot_manifests():
+    return {name:sha(CAND.parent/'snapshots'/name/'manifest.sha256') for name in read(PREP/'all-snapshots-verified.json')}

+    assert state(INTEGRATION,True)==before['integration']
+    assert metadata(INTEGRATION)==before['integration_metadata']
+    assert state(CAND,True)==before['candidate']
+    assert metadata(CAND)==before['candidate_metadata']
+    assert snapshot_manifests()==before['snapshot_manifests']

+    assert text(MAIN,'rev-parse',SECOND+'^')==FIRST
+    assert before['integration']['head']==SECOND and before['integration']['head_tree']==FINAL_TREE
+    assert before['integration']['branch']==BRANCH and not before['integration']['status']
+    assert text(MAIN,'rev-parse','refs/heads/'+BRANCH)==SECOND

## Validation

Validation scope follows REGRESSION RISK, never line count, file count, or file extension alone. The alignment manifest and the language rules decide which semantic EDITS a change needs (Lean, C#, corpus, docs); this section decides how much local validation the candidate gets and how it is executed. `.github/workflows/validate.yml` stays the full .NET + Lean backstop for pull requests and pushes to `main`: a local V0–V2 omission is a deliberate risk decision, and CI is never a reason to skip V3 locally. It IS the reason a local V1/V2 stays bounded: the backstop catches what a scoped run misses, so a V1/V2 run is never padded with a full phase "to be safe".

### Candidate and level

- Assess the COMPLETE candidate: the relevant commits plus staged, unstaged, untracked, deleted, and renamed files. A clean working tree is not evidence that a committed candidate needs no tests. Preserve unrelated work and account for it when it affects the candidate or the test results.
- Classify by semantic impact, dependency reach, and changed contracts. Start at V1 unless the change is clearly V0, then apply the V2/V3 triggers; when the impact cannot be confidently bounded, choose V3. Record the level and a one-line reason before validation starts; the level may be raised on evidence, never lowered. The level is also the execution plan: V0–V2 run only what their row names, and the full `validate-all.ps1` phases belong to V3 alone — if the candidate warrants a full phase, record V3; running one at V1/V2 is a misclassification, not extra diligence.

| Level | Appropriate scope | Required local validation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| V0 — trivial | Instruction/prose edits, comments, or formatting proven not to affect execution or mechanically checked content | Review the diff, whitespace (`git diff --check`), and the references/consistency of the text. No build or runtime suite for a genuinely documentation-only change. |
| V1 — focused | Small, isolated, behavior-preserving refactor or test change with a well-understood dependency boundary | Build the affected project/test dependency closure; run the directly related tests with verified filters. |
| V2 — affected | Bounded subsystem behavior change; a limited shared helper, API, or diagnostic contract change; neighboring consumers affected | Focused tests plus the neighboring/affected suites, the affected project builds, and the applicable parity/artifact/Lean checks — never the full solution suite or a `validate-all.ps1` phase. |
| V3 — full | Fundamental behavior, broadly shared infrastructure, cross-cutting changes, or uncertain impact | Complete local .NET validation and all seven canonical Lean targets, plus any specifically required regression/parity checks. |

V3 is MANDATORY for changes to parser/grammar behavior or AST structure; elaboration; lexical ownership/name resolution; parameter binding or implicit lifting; Grace; sequence/list/spread/collect/arity semantics; the evaluator core; the optimizer/planned execution; sync/async/cancellation behavior; core loading/module semantics; caching/exposure; Decimal128/numeric semantics; Lean/C# correspondence; and widely reused infrastructure or build/toolchain changes with broad impact. The triggers concern the behavior or machinery changed: a comment fix inside `Parser.cs` is not V3, a one-line ownership fix is; a formatting-only string-construction refactor may be V1 when the output contract is demonstrably unchanged; updating expected semantic results never makes a semantic change test-only. V2 covers bounded production-behavior changes, shared consumers, and API/diagnostic contracts without a V3 trigger — an isolated CLI presentation change needs no evaluator-wide validation, a change to shared loading or cancellation does. Executable documentation is not prose: tutorial result claims, spec-linked examples, generated prompt blocks, and the EBNF keep their verification tests (coverage map below) even when only text files changed, so such a change is neither automatically V0 nor V3; changed language MEANING is still V3 plus the semantic-update process.

### Lean validation

- V3 always runs all seven Lean targets, even when no `.lean` file changed — a C#-only optimizer, async, or ownership change is V3, and `SemanticExplorerCases`/`LanguageSpecCases` are how Lean/C# correspondence is checked.
- V1/V2: build the affected Lean targets and the dependent artifact/parity checks whenever Lean code, proofs, guards, imports, or generated Lean content changes or is affected; a meaningful Lean-only change never gets zero Lean validation, and unclear dependency reach means V3. Pure Lean comments may be V0; regenerating an artifact without a content change is not itself a semantic change.

### Commands

The normal V3 command, from the repo root:

```powershell
pwsh -NoProfile -File ./scripts/validate-all.ps1 -Phase All
```

Its .NET phase runs the FULL solution build (every project — `dotnet test` alone builds only test projects and their dependencies, so benchmark/demo compile breaks escape it), then the C# suite with `--no-build`, then `git diff --check`; its Lean phase owns the one canonical seven-target list. The script accepts only `All` (the default), `DotNet`, and `Lean` (plus `-ForceInvocationPlans`, below): it has no focused or level switch and does not detect risk. Completing `-Phase DotNet` and then `-Phase Lean`, one after the other, against the same unchanged candidate satisfies V3 — do not rerun `All` merely to repeat completed work, and never run the two phases side by side — while a partial phase alone is never full validation. A phase already runs every focused suite, so it is never preceded, accompanied, or followed by a separate filtered pass over the same candidate. Each phase fingerprints the staged, unstaged, and untracked state and fails if validation changes it; a checkout may start dirty, but validation must leave it exactly as it started.

FORCED INVOCATION-PLAN RUN: `pwsh -NoProfile -File ./scripts/validate-all.ps1 -Phase DotNet -ForceInvocationPlans` runs the same .NET phase with `KATLANG_FORCE_INVOCATION_PLANS=1` set before any test host starts (`ForcedInvocationPlansHook`, read once at test-assembly load), so every evaluator run of `KatLang.Tests` retains invocation plans and every call-shaped supplied argument takes the plan route; the ordinary phase REMOVES an inherited flag. It is a different execution mode, not a repeated pass, and it must pass in full: a change to invocation plans, call references/META, the J7 plan-retention gate, or supplied-cell/need binding runs it after its V3 `-Phase DotNet`. A route-dependent expectation (plan/supply-formation counts, `RetainsInvocationPlans`, plan-disabled fusion hits) selects between its two independently justified expectations with `ForcedInvocationPlansHook.Forced`; values, effects, charges and diagnostics never depend on the mode. Manual equivalent: set or remove the variable in the CHILD process environment, never with `Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable` inside a test.

Manual .NET fallback (equivalent, including the independent full-solution build):

```powershell
dotnet build .\KatLang.slnx -p:UseSharedCompilation=false
dotnet test .\KatLang.slnx -p:UseSharedCompilation=false --no-build
git diff --check
```

Manual Lean fallback (all seven targets — V3, or a V1/V2 change that affects Lean):

```powershell
Push-Location .\lean
lake build CoreTests
lake build KatLangArityLaws
lake build AstDemo
lake build CoreArityAlgebra
lake build CoreArityAlgebraProofs
lake build SemanticExplorerCases
lake build LanguageSpecCases
Pop-Location
```

Lean CoreTests use `#guard` for semantic assertions, so a failing assertion fails `lake build CoreTests`. Remaining `#eval` lines are demo/inspection output only.

Focused V1/V2 runs build the affected projects, then filter, for example:

```powershell
dotnet build ./tests/KatLang.Tests/KatLang.Tests.csproj -p:UseSharedCompilation=false
dotnet test ./tests/KatLang.Tests/KatLang.Tests.csproj -p:UseSharedCompilation=false --no-build --filter "FullyQualifiedName~SameLineSeparatorTests"
```

Filters must name real test classes/namespaces (check the inventory: the class in `LanguageSpec/GeneratorSpecTests.cs` is `LanguageSpecArtifactsGeneratorPromptTests`), and the summary must show the intended tests discovered AND executed — zero matching tests is not a pass whatever the exit code. Use `--no-build` only after a successful, current build of the same projects/configuration/framework and inputs. Verification outside the script keeps its guarantees: neutralize inherited `KATLANG_REGENERATE_*` flags for the verification process only (a child `pwsh -NoProfile` whose environment is discarded, never the caller's lasting environment), snapshot `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all` plus the index and worktree diffs before and after, and report an unexpected mutation with its evidence instead of undoing it. Keep terminal output minimal; save complete stdout/stderr under the ignored `artifacts/validation/` directory or a temporary directory, preserving the command's real exit code when redirecting or piping (`$LASTEXITCODE` after the native command in pwsh, `pipefail`/`PIPESTATUS` in bash). Missing required tooling (SDK, `lake`, a runner) is BLOCKED/incomplete validation, never a pass and never a silently lower level.

### Regenerating generated artifacts

Generated artifacts are never edited by hand and never rewritten by a verification run. Regeneration is one deliberate, targeted `dotnet test` run with the artifact's flag set to `1`: the run WRITES the artifact and then FAILS BY DESIGN (also when nothing changed), so it can never pass as verification — review the diff, clear the flag, and run the normal verification at the level the underlying change requires (an intentional language-behavior change is V3).

| Artifact | Flag | Filter |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lean/LanguageSpecCases.lean` plus the `=== BEGIN GENERATED: katlang-spec-examples ===` block in `.github/agents/katlang-generator.agent.md` and `experimental/prompts/katlang-generator.txt` | `KATLANG_REGENERATE_LANGUAGE_SPEC` | `--filter LanguageSpecArtifacts` |
| `lean/SemanticExplorerCases.lean` | `KATLANG_REGENERATE_SEMANTIC_EXPLORER` | `--filter SemanticExplorerLeanArtifact` |
| `tests/KatLang.Formatting.PublicApi.Tests/PublicApiBaseline.txt` | `KATLANG_REGENERATE_PUBLIC_API` | `--filter PublicApiBaseline` |
| `lean/CoreTests/HostParentDifferential.lean` | `KATLANG_REGENERATE_HOST_PARENT_DIFFERENTIAL` | `--filter HostParentDifferential` |

For example `$env:KATLANG_REGENERATE_LANGUAGE_SPEC = "1"; dotnet test .\KatLang.slnx --filter LanguageSpecArtifacts`. `validate-all.ps1` is observational: before it builds or tests anything it removes every `KATLANG_REGENERATE_*` variable from its own process (the whole prefix, case-insensitively; restored on exit), so an inherited flag can never make a green run rewrite a tracked artifact. The flag registry and the write-then-fail contract are `RegenerationFlags` / `ArtifactRegeneration` in `tests/KatLang.Tests/Infrastructure/ArtifactRegeneration.cs` (shared as source with the public-API test project); a new `KATLANG_REGENERATE_*` variable must be registered there — `ArtifactRegenerationPolicyTests` scans the repository for unregistered names and for tests that read a flag outside the helper.

### Execution discipline

Validation is executed by the primary agent, in ONE execution stream: never two of `dotnet build`, `dotnet test`, `lake build`, a `validate-all.ps1` phase, or a regeneration run in flight at once — concurrent `dotnet test` invocations lock `KatLang.Tests.dll` (MSB3027), a phase fingerprints the tree while it runs, and a second run of the same suite over an unchanged candidate is pure duplication. Every command's full output goes to a log file (the ignored `artifacts/validation/` directory or a temporary directory) and only its summary lines — result totals, failure identities, exit code — are read back, never the whole log.

- ONE plan per candidate, chosen before anything runs: at V1/V2 the focused and affected suites, most informative first, and nothing beyond them; at V3 the full phases only. Development checks while editing stay minimal — the test class being written, `scripts/check-cancellation-token-order.ps1` after a signature change (`Coding Guidance`), the one previously failing check after a repair, the Lean target that compiles the edited file, a regeneration run — because the plan runs everything else exactly once; a pre-validation sweep of neighboring suites runs every test twice.
- One command at a time, waited to completion: a `--no-build` run only after the build's exit code is in hand, `lake build` never beside a `dotnet` command, the .NET phase and then the Lean phase, never side by side. A `validate-all.ps1` phase exceeds the foreground time limit, so run it as ONE background command and then wait for its completion — no polling loop (every poll re-reads the whole context), no other command, and no edit to the checkout until it has finished.
- On a failure, capture the command, the failure identity, and the evidence; decide what it means; repair; rerun only the failing check; then complete the plan for the FINAL candidate. Reuse earlier results only while their inputs, dependencies, configuration, and environment still apply (later prose-only edits do not by themselves invalidate runtime results). When a failure suggests wider regression, or the diff reveals a V3 trigger the classification missed, raise the scope one level at a time — never as a precaution — and a full phase replaces the remaining focused plan instead of adding to it. Do not rerun an unchanged failure repeatedly, and do not launch every suite to diagnose a missing SDK.
- Never claim validation from a partial run, a stale build, an unexecuted command, a zero-test filter, or an assumption that CI will pass, and do not label a failure pre-existing or flaky without evidence. Report what ran, the counts, the failures, what was omitted and why, and the log paths.

### Subagents

Do not delegate test execution. Measured in September 2026, a validation worker spent 30–50 requests to run two or three commands — about ten times the cost of running them inline — could not work in parallel with a tree that must stay frozen, and shared no prompt cache with the primary agent (caches are model-scoped and prefix-exact). A subagent is for a BULKY, SELF-CONTAINED INVESTIGATION whose intermediate reading would otherwise flood the primary context — a failure hunt across many files, an inventory, a cross-file audit. Give it the cheapest model that can do the job, a bounded brief with an explicit stopping point, and ask for `file:line` facts; code the primary agent will edit or reason about it reads itself, in bounded ranges. Never spawn one for a single known file, and never let one edit, regenerate, or validate.

## Validation

Validation scope follows REGRESSION RISK, never line count, file count, or file extension alone. The alignment manifest and the language rules decide which semantic EDITS a change needs (Lean, C#, corpus, docs); this section decides how much local validation the candidate gets and how it is executed. `.github/workflows/validate.yml` stays the full .NET + Lean backstop for pull requests and pushes to `main`: a local V0–V2 omission is a deliberate risk decision, and CI is never a reason to skip V3 locally. It IS the reason a local V1/V2 stays bounded: the backstop catches what a scoped run misses, so a V1/V2 run is never padded with a full phase "to be safe".

### Candidate and level

- Assess the COMPLETE candidate: the relevant commits plus staged, unstaged, untracked, deleted, and renamed files. A clean working tree is not evidence that a committed candidate needs no tests. Preserve unrelated work and account for it when it affects the candidate or the test results.
- Classify by semantic impact, dependency reach, and changed contracts. Start at V1 unless the change is clearly V0, then apply the V2/V3 triggers; when the impact cannot be confidently bounded, choose V3. Record the level and a one-line reason before validation starts; the level may be raised on evidence, never lowered. The level is also the execution plan: V0–V2 run only what their row names, and the full `validate-all.ps1` phases belong to V3 alone — if the candidate warrants a full phase, record V3; running one at V1/V2 is a misclassification, not extra diligence.

| Level | Appropriate scope | Required local validation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| V0 — trivial | Instruction/prose edits, comments, or formatting proven not to affect execution or mechanically checked content | Review the diff, whitespace (`git diff --check`), and the references/consistency of the text. No build or runtime suite for a genuinely documentation-only change. |
| V1 — focused | Small, isolated, behavior-preserving refactor or test change with a well-understood dependency boundary | Build the affected project/test dependency closure; run the directly related tests with verified filters. |
| V2 — affected | Bounded subsystem behavior change; a limited shared helper, API, or diagnostic contract change; neighboring consumers affected | Focused tests plus the neighboring/affected suites, the affected project builds, and the applicable parity/artifact/Lean checks — never the full solution suite or a `validate-all.ps1` phase. |
| V3 — full | Fundamental behavior, broadly shared infrastructure, cross-cutting changes, or uncertain impact | Complete local .NET validation and all seven canonical Lean targets, plus any specifically required regression/parity checks. |

V3 is MANDATORY for changes to parser/grammar behavior or AST structure; elaboration; lexical ownership/name resolution; parameter binding or implicit lifting; Grace; sequence/list/spread/collect/arity semantics; the evaluator core; the optimizer/planned execution; sync/async/cancellation behavior; core loading/module semantics; caching/exposure; Decimal128/numeric semantics; Lean/C# correspondence; and widely reused infrastructure or build/toolchain changes with broad impact. The triggers concern the behavior or machinery changed: a comment fix inside `Parser.cs` is not V3, a one-line ownership fix is; a formatting-only string-construction refactor may be V1 when the output contract is demonstrably unchanged; updating expected semantic results never makes a semantic change test-only. V2 covers bounded production-behavior changes, shared consumers, and API/diagnostic contracts without a V3 trigger — an isolated CLI presentation change needs no evaluator-wide validation, a change to shared loading or cancellation does. Executable documentation is not prose: tutorial result claims, spec-linked examples, generated prompt blocks, and the EBNF keep their verification tests (coverage map below) even when only text files changed, so such a change is neither automatically V0 nor V3; changed language MEANING is still V3 plus the semantic-update process.

### Lean validation

- V3 always runs all seven Lean targets, even when no `.lean` file changed — a C#-only optimizer, async, or ownership change is V3, and `SemanticExplorerCases`/`LanguageSpecCases` are how Lean/C# correspondence is checked.
- V1/V2: build the affected Lean targets and the dependent artifact/parity checks whenever Lean code, proofs, guards, imports, or generated Lean content changes or is affected; a meaningful Lean-only change never gets zero Lean validation, and unclear dependency reach means V3. Pure Lean comments may be V0; regenerating an artifact without a content change is not itself a semantic change.

### Commands

The normal V3 command, from the repo root:

```powershell
pwsh -NoProfile -File ./scripts/validate-all.ps1 -Phase All
```

Its .NET phase runs the FULL solution build (every project — `dotnet test` alone builds only test projects and their dependencies, so benchmark/demo compile breaks escape it), then the C# suite with `--no-build`, then `git diff --check`; its Lean phase owns the one canonical seven-target list. tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.
